states.name: Rajasthan
states.overview: The Land of Kings, world-renowned for invincible desert fortresses, royal Havelis, vibrant folk rhythms, and centuries of chivalric Rajput heritage.
states.culture_desc: Rich folklore rooted in chivalry, Ghoomar and Kalbelia dance forms, Kathputli puppetry, and vibrant turbans reflecting distinct clan lineages.
states.festivals_desc: Pushkar Camel Fair, Teej, Gangaur, Jaisalmer Desert Festival, and Jaipur Literature Festival celebrated with spectacular royal pageantry.
states.food_desc: Arid climate cuisine rich in ghee and milk: Dal Baati Churma, Ker Sangri, Gatte ki Sabzi, Laal Maas, and Ghevar sweets.
states.languages_desc: Hindi (official), Rajasthani, Marwari, Mewari, Dhundhari, and Harauti.
states.art_crafts_desc: Blue Pottery of Jaipur, Bagru & Sanganeri block print textiles, Pichwai paintings of Nathdwara, Kundan-Meenakari jewellery, and Mojari leathercraft.

states.name: Kerala
states.overview: Known as God's Own Country, blessed with emerald backwaters, spice-scented hills, ancient Ayurvedic healing traditions, and classical temple arts.
states.culture_desc: Kathakali classical dance-drama, ritualistic Theyyam performances, Kalaripayattu martial art (oldest in the world), and matrilineal heritage.
states.festivals_desc: Onam harvest festival with floral Pookkalams and Vallam Kali snake boat races, and Thrissur Pooram with majestic temple percussion ensembles.
states.food_desc: Coconut and pepper-forward coastal delicacies: Kerala Sadya feast on banana leaf, Appam with Stew, Malabar Biryani, and Karimeen Pollichathu.
states.languages_desc: Malayalam (official, classical language) and English.
states.art_crafts_desc: Aranmula Kannadi metal mirrors, Kasavu gold-bordered handlooms, Nettoor Petti rosewood jewelry boxes, and coir handicraft.

states.name: Tamil Nadu
states.overview: Cradle of ancient Dravidian civilization, celebrated for colossal towering temple gopurams, millennia-old Tamil literature, and Carnatic music.
states.culture_desc: Bharatanatyam classical dance, sacred Chola bronze sculpting, Margazhi musical season, and classical Sangam literary heritage.
states.festivals_desc: Pongal harvest celebration, Chithirai festival of Madurai, Natyanjali dance festival, and Karthigai Deepam of Tiruvannamalai.
states.food_desc: Fragrant South Indian heritage: Idli, Dosa, Sambar, Chettinad Pepper Chicken, Filter Coffee, and Tirunelveli Halwa.
states.languages_desc: Tamil (one of the oldest surviving classical languages in the world) and English.
states.art_crafts_desc: Tanjore gold-foil paintings, Kanchipuram pure silk sarees, Swamimalai lost-wax bronze sculptures, and Pattamadai mats.

states.name: Uttar Pradesh
states.overview: Heartland of Indian spiritual philosophy, cradle of the Ganges civilization, home to the immortal Taj Mahal, Varanasi ghats, and royal Awadhi elegance.
states.culture_desc: Kathak classical dance, Lucknowi Tehzeeb (refined court etiquette), Kabir spiritual poetry, and classical Hindustani music gharanas.
states.festivals_desc: Kumbh Mela (largest spiritual gathering on Earth), Lathmar Holi of Barsana, Dev Deepawali in Varanasi, and Ganga Dussehra.
states.food_desc: Nawabi Awadhi and Braj cuisine: Galouti Kebabs, Lucknowi Dum Biryani, Bedmi Puri, Banarasi Paan, and Makhan Malai.
states.languages_desc: Hindi (official), Urdu, Awadhi, Bhojpuri, and Braj Bhasha.
states.art_crafts_desc: Lucknowi Chikankari hand embroidery, Varanasi Zari and Banarasi brocade silks, Brassware of Moradabad, and Kannauj natural perfumes (Ittar).

states.name: Maharashtra
states.overview: Land of warrior king Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, UNESCO rock-cut cave monuments of Ajanta & Ellora, and Sahyadri hill citadels.
states.culture_desc: Lavani folk dance, Powada martial ballads, Warkari devotional pilgrimage tradition, and vibrant theatre.
states.festivals_desc: Ganeshotsav celebrated with grand Dhol-Tasha processions, Gudi Padwa, and Narali Purnima.
states.food_desc: Maharashtrian comfort cuisine: Puran Poli, Misal Pav, Vada Pav, Thalipeeth, Pithla Bhakri, and Konkani Sol Kadhi.
states.languages_desc: Marathi (official, classical status) and Konkani.
states.art_crafts_desc: Warli tribal painting, Paithani silk sarees with peacock pallu, Kolhapuri handcrafted chappals, and Sawantwadi wooden toys.

states.name: West Bengal
states.overview: Cultural and intellectual capital of the Bengal Renaissance, celebrated for Rabindrasangeet, terracotta temples, and UNESCO Durga Puja.
states.culture_desc: Baul mystic songs, literary adda tradition, Rabindra Sangeet, Chau martial masked dance, and rich cinematic heritage.
states.festivals_desc: Durga Puja (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage), Poila Boishakh (Bengali New Year), Saraswati Puja, and Ganga Sagar Mela.
states.food_desc: Subtle culinary symphony: Macher Jhol, Shorshe Ilish, Kosha Mangsho, Luchi-Alur Dom, Sandesh, and legendary Rosogolla.
states.languages_desc: Bengali (official) and English.
states.art_crafts_desc: Terracotta temples of Bishnupur, Dokra lost-wax metal craft, Baluchari silk sarees, Kantha embroidery, and Kalighat folk art.

states.name: Gujarat
states.overview: Land of historic Harappan ports, subterranean stepwells, Mahatma Gandhi’s philosophy of Ahimsa, and dazzling textiles.
states.culture_desc: Garba and Dandiya Raas (UNESCO Intangible Heritage), Dayro folk storytelling, and rich pastoral nomadic traditions.
states.festivals_desc: Navratri (world’s longest dance festival), Rann Utsav in white salt desert, and Uttarayan International Kite Festival.
states.food_desc: Sweet, savory, and spiced vegetarian gastronomy: Gujarati Thali, Dhokla, Khandvi, Thepla, Undhiyu, and Fafda-Jalebi.
states.languages_desc: Gujarati (official) and Kutchi.
states.art_crafts_desc: Patan Patola double-ikat weaving, Rogan art of Nirona, Bandhani tie-dye, and intricate Kutch mirrorwork embroidery.

states.name: Karnataka
states.overview: Empire of Vijayanagara ruins at Hampi, Hoysala star-shaped temples, sacred sandalwood forests, and exquisite silk craftsmanship.
states.culture_desc: Yakshagana mythological theatre, Carnatic musical traditions, Dollu Kunitha drum dance, and royal Mysuru heritage.
states.festivals_desc: Mysuru Dasara featuring the golden howdah procession, Kambala buffalo race, Hampi Utsav, and Karaga festival.
states.food_desc: Rich Kannada fare: Bisi Bele Bath, Mysore Masala Dosa, Mysore Pak, Ragi Mudde, Mangalorean Ghee Roast, and filter coffee.
states.languages_desc: Kannada (official classical language), Tulu, and Kodava.
states.art_crafts_desc: Mysore Sandalwood carving, Ilkal and Mysore silk sarees, Bidriware silver-inlaid metalcraft, and Channapatna wooden lacquer toys.

states.name: Madhya Pradesh
states.overview: The geographic heart of India, home to Khajuraho temples, Emperor Ashoka’s Sanchi Stupa, prehistoric Bhimbetka caves, and tiger sanctuaries.
states.culture_desc: Ancient tribal Gond and Bhil lore, Malwa classical traditions, Tansen music heritage of Gwalior, and Matki folk dance.
states.festivals_desc: Khajuraho Dance Festival, Tansen Sangeet Samaroh, Mandu Festival, and Bhagoria Haat tribal fair.
states.food_desc: Central Indian culinary flavors: Poha Jalebi, Bhutte Ka Kees, Dal Bafla, Rogan Josh of Bhopal, and Mawa Bati sweet.
states.languages_desc: Hindi (official), Malwi, Nimadi, Bundeli, and Bagheli.
states.art_crafts_desc: Chanderi handloom sarees, Maheshwari woven silks, Gond tribal paintings, and Bagh traditional woodblock printing.

states.name: Odisha
states.overview: Land of Lord Jagannath, colossal Sun Temple of Konark designed as a stone chariot, classical Odissi dance, and ancient Kalinga architecture.
states.culture_desc: Odissi classical dance, Gotipua acrobatics, Jagannath temple Mahaprasad rituals, and ancient maritime Bali Jatra lore.
states.festivals_desc: Puri Rath Yatra (Chariot Festival), Konark Dance Festival, Raja Parba honoring Mother Earth, and Durga Puja.
states.food_desc: Pure sattvic temple gastronomy: Chhena Poda (baked caramelized cheese), Dalma lentil stew, Khaja sweet, and Pakhala Bhata.
states.languages_desc: Odia (official classical language) and Santali.
states.art_crafts_desc: Pattachitra scroll paintings on palm leaf, Cuttack silver filigree (Tarakasi), Pipili applique patchwork, and Sambalpuri Ikat textiles.

states.name: Punjab
states.overview: The Land of Five Rivers, sanctified by the Golden Temple of Amritsar, valorous Sikh history, vibrant agrarian energy, and joyous hospitality.
states.culture_desc: Bhangra and Giddha energetic folk dances, Gatka martial arts, Sufi poetry of Bulleh Shah and Waris Shah, and community Langar ethos.
states.festivals_desc: Baisakhi harvest festival, Lohri bonfire celebration, Hola Mohalla martial festival at Anandpur Sahib, and Gurpurabs.
states.food_desc: Rich tandoori and farm-fresh cuisine: Makki di Roti with Sarson da Saag, Butter Chicken, Dal Makhani, Amritsari Kulcha, and Lassi.
states.languages_desc: Punjabi (official, written in Gurmukhi script) and Hindi.
states.art_crafts_desc: Phulkari floral geometric hand embroidery, Punjabi Juttis, woodwork of Kartarpur, and Brass utensil making of Jandiala Guru (UNESCO).

states.name: Himachal Pradesh
states.overview: Devbhumi (Land of the Gods), nestled in the snow-capped Himalayas, ancient timber-and-stone Kath Kuni temples, and Buddhist monasteries.
states.culture_desc: Nati community folk dance (Guinness record holder), Kullu shawls weaving, and Himalayan village deity governance traditions.
states.festivals_desc: Kullu Dussehra week-long congregation of village deities, Minjar Fair of Chamba, and Losar Tibetan New Year in Spiti.
states.food_desc: Pahari culinary heritage: Dham festive feast, Siddu steamed wheat bread with walnut paste, Babru, and Chha Gosht.
states.languages_desc: Hindi (official), Pahari, Kangri, Mandiali, and Kinnauri.
states.art_crafts_desc: Kullu and Kinnauri woolen shawls, Chamba Rumal miniature needlework, Kangra miniature painting, and Tibetan Thangka scrolls.

states.name: Andhra Pradesh
states.overview: Home of the sacred Tirumala Venkateswara Temple, ancient Buddhist sites of Amaravati, classical Kuchipudi dance, and spice-rich coastal culture.
states.culture_desc: Kuchipudi classical dance, Harikatha storytelling, Burra Katha folk music, and grand Telugu literary heritage.
states.festivals_desc: Ugadi (Telugu New Year), Brahmotsavam of Tirupati, Sankranti with cock-fights and Haridasu songs, and Visakha Utsav.
states.food_desc: Fiery Andhra and Rayalaseema gastronomy: Andhra Bhojanam, Gongura Pachadi, Pesarattu with Upma, Royyala Iguru, and Pootharekulu sweet.
states.languages_desc: Telugu (classical language, "Italian of the East") and Urdu.
states.art_crafts_desc: Kalamkari hand-painted temple textiles of Srikalahasti, Kondapalli and Etikoppaka wooden lacquer toys, and Machilipatnam brassware.

states.name: Telangana
states.overview: Land of historic Kakatiya architecture, Charminar, Golconda diamonds, Bathukamma floral traditions, and regal Deccan gastronomy.
states.culture_desc: Perini Sivatandavam warrior dance, Dakhni language, Deccani miniature painting, and Qutb Shahi royal patronage.
states.festivals_desc: Bathukamma floral celebration of feminine spirit, Bonalu honoring Goddess Mahakali, and Medaram Jatara (largest tribal congregation).
states.food_desc: Regal Hyderabadi and Telangana cuisine: Hyderabadi Dum Biryani, Mirchi ka Salan, Haleem, Sarva Pindi, and Double ka Meetha.
states.languages_desc: Telugu (official), Urdu, and Dakhni.
states.art_crafts_desc: Pochampally Ikat tie-and-dye silks, Bidriware of Hyderabad, Pembarthi metalcraft, and Cheriyal scroll paintings.

states.name: Assam
states.overview: The Land of the Red River and Blue Hills, famous for one-horned rhinos of Kaziranga, holy Kamakhya Temple, Majuli river island, and lush tea gardens.
states.culture_desc: Sattriya classical dance, Bihu energetic folk dances, Borgeet devotional hymns composed by Srimanta Sankardev, and bell-metal heritage.
states.festivals_desc: Rongali Bihu (celebrating spring renewal), Kongali Bihu, Bhogali Bihu, Ambubachi Mela at Kamakhya, and Majuli Raas Mahotsav.
states.food_desc: Mild, aromatic Assamese flavors: Khaar traditional alkaline dish, Masor Tenga sour fish curry, Duck with Ash Gourd, and Pitha rice cakes.
states.languages_desc: Assamese (official, classical status), Bodo, and Bengali.
states.art_crafts_desc: Muga Golden Silk (indigenous only to Assam), Eri and Pat silks, Bell-metal craft of Sarthebari, and bamboo cane artifacts of Majuli.

states.name: Bihar
states.overview: Cradle of ancient empires (Maurya and Gupta), birthplace of Buddhism and Jainism, home to Nalanda University (UNESCO) and Bodh Gaya.
states.culture_desc: Ancient Buddhist Dhammachakka philosophy, Bidesia folk theatre of Bhikhari Thakur, and centuries-old Vedic traditions.
states.festivals_desc: Chhath Puja (ancient sun-worship festival of purity), Sonepur Cattle Fair, Pitrapaksha Mela of Gaya, and Buddha Jayanti.
states.food_desc: Wholesome rustic cuisine: Litti Chokha baked over cow-dung embers, Sattu Paratha, Bihari Kebab, Khaja of Silao, and Tilkut.
states.languages_desc: Hindi (official), Maithili (scheduled language), Bhojpuri, Magahi, and Angika.
states.art_crafts_desc: Madhubani (Mithila) folk paintings, Sujani needlework embroidery, Sikki grass weaving, and Manjusha scroll art.

states.name: Uttarakhand
states.overview: Devbhoomi (Land of the Gods), origin of the holy rivers Ganga and Yamuna, home to the sacred Char Dham and UNESCO Nanda Devi & Valley of Flowers.
states.culture_desc: Choliya sword dance of Kumaon, Jhora and Chanchari folk songs, Ramman religious masked theatre (UNESCO), and sacred Himalayan pilgrim traditions.
states.festivals_desc: Kumbh Mela at Haridwar, Nanda Devi Raj Jat pilgrimage, Ganga Dussehra, and Phool Dei spring flower festival.
states.food_desc: Nutritious mountain cuisine: Kafuli spinach-fenugreek stew, Chainsoo roasted black gram curry, Bhatt ki Churkani, and Bal Mithai sweet of Almora.
states.languages_desc: Hindi (official), Sanskrit (second official), Garhwali, Kumaoni, and Jaunsari.
states.art_crafts_desc: Aipan geometric ritual floor and wall art, Ringal bamboo craft, Woodcarving of Kumaoni doors (Kholi), and woolen Thulma blankets.

states.name: Jammu and Kashmir
states.overview: Paradise on Earth, celebrated for emerald Dal Lake, snow-draped Pir Panjal ranges, Mughal gardens, holy Vaishno Devi shrine, and Sufi mysticism.
states.culture_desc: Rouf and Bhand Pather folk dances, Sufiyana Kalam music, Dogra martial lore, and centuries of syncretic Kashmiriyat harmony.
states.festivals_desc: Tulip Festival of Srinagar, Shikara Festival, Jhiri Mela in Jammu, and Eid celebrated with traditional culinary feasts.
states.food_desc: Royal Kashmiri Wazwan multi-course feast: Rogan Josh, Gushtaba, Yakhni, Dum Aloo, Nadru Yakhni, and fragrant Kahwa saffron tea.
states.languages_desc: Kashmiri, Dogri, Hindi, Urdu, and Gojri.
states.art_crafts_desc: Pashmina hand-spun shawls with Sozni needlework, Kashmiri Papier-Mache, Walnut wood carving, and hand-knotted silk carpets.

states.name: Ladakh
states.overview: The Land of High Passes, high-altitude desert surrounded by the Karakoram and Himalayas, ancient Tibetan Buddhist monasteries, and crystal lakes.
states.culture_desc: Cham sacred monastic mask dances, ancient Bon and Buddhist scriptures, Losar New Year celebrations, and polo played on mountain ponies.
states.festivals_desc: Hemis Festival honoring Guru Padmasambhava, Ladakh Festival, Dosmochey festival of the scapegoat, and Sindhu Darshan.
states.food_desc: Hearty Himalayan diet: Thukpa noodle soup, Steamed Momos, Skyu root vegetable stew, Tsampa roasted barley flour, and Gur-Gur salty butter tea.
states.languages_desc: Ladakhi (Bhoti), Balti, Hindi, and English.
states.art_crafts_desc: Thangka silk scroll paintings, Ladakhi Pashmina spinning, Woodblock monastic printing, and traditional silver Pperak headdresses.

states.name: Goa
states.overview: Sun-drenched coastal state renowned for UNESCO Portuguese-era basilicas, serene golden beaches, Konkani folk culture, and Indo-Portuguese lifestyle.
states.culture_desc: Mando romantic song-dance, Dhalo and Fugdi folk dances, vibrant Tiatr theatre, and centuries of Latin-Hindu cultural synthesis.
states.festivals_desc: Goa Carnival with flamboyant street floats, Shigmo spring festival, Feast of St. Francis Xavier at Old Goa, and Sao Joao well-jumping.
states.food_desc: Indo-Portuguese coastal flavors: Goan Fish Curry with rice, Pork Vindaloo, Chicken Xacuti, Pao bread, Feni liquor, and Bebinca multi-layered dessert.
states.languages_desc: Konkani (official language, written in Devanagari), Marathi, and English.
states.art_crafts_desc: Azulejos glazed hand-painted ceramic tiles, Seashell craft, Brass lamp casting, and coconut shell carvings.

states.name: Haryana
states.overview: Land of Kurukshetra where the Bhagavad Gita was expounded, ancient Indus Valley sites of Rakhigarhi, agrarian prosperity, and Olympic sporting legends.
states.culture_desc: Ragini folk music battles, Saang musical folk theatre, Dhamal and Ghoomar dances, and strong agrarian joint family values.
states.festivals_desc: Surajkund International Crafts Mela, Gita Jayanti Samaroh in Kurukshetra, Baisakhi, and Teej celebrations.
states.food_desc: Dairy and grain-rich cuisine: Bajra Khichdi with ghee, Makhan and Lassi, Kadhi Pakora, Kachri ki Sabzi, and Malpua.
states.languages_desc: Hindi (official), Haryanvi (Bangru), Ahirwati, and Punjabi.
states.art_crafts_desc: Phulkari embroidery of Rohtak, Panipat handloom durries and carpets, Terracotta pottery of Jhajjar, and brassware of Rewari.

states.name: Jharkhand
states.overview: The Land of Forests and Waterfalls, sacred Baidyanath Jyotirlinga, rich tribal heritage of Santhal, Munda, and Oraon communities, and mineral wealth.
states.culture_desc: Chhau martial mask dance, Jhumair and Karma folk dances, Sohrai pastoral festival, and deep revered connection to the Sal sacred groves (Sarna).
states.festivals_desc: Sarhul (worship of the blooming Sal trees), Karma festival, Sohrai cattle festival, and Shravani Mela at Deoghar.
states.food_desc: Rustic tribal gastronomy: Dhuska deep-fried rice-lentil bread, Rugra wild mushrooms, Bamboo shoot curry, Handia rice beverage, and Thekua.
states.languages_desc: Hindi (official), Santhali, Mundari, Ho, Kurukh, Khortha, and Nagpuri.
states.art_crafts_desc: Sohrai and Khovar wall mural paintings (GI-tagged), Dokra lost-wax brass castings, Paitkar scroll paintings, and wooden tribal masks.

states.name: Chhattisgarh
states.overview: The Rice Bowl of India, home to the legendary Dandakaranya forest, Chitrakote Falls (Niagara of India), Bastar tribal arts, and Bhoramdeo temple.
states.culture_desc: Panthi spiritual dance of Satnami community, Pandavani musical narration of Mahabharata by Teejan Bai, and Bastar tribal rituals.
states.festivals_desc: Bastar Dussehra (world’s longest 75-day festival dedicated to Goddess Danteshwari), Madai tribal festival, and Rajim Kumbh Mela.
states.food_desc: Wholesome rice-based recipes: Chila rice pancakes, Fara steamed dumplings, Muthia, Aamat vegetable stew, and Mahua flower beverages.
states.languages_desc: Hindi (official), Chhattisgarhi, Gondi, and Halbi.
states.art_crafts_desc: Bastar Bell Metal (Dhokra) craft, Wrought Iron (Loha Shilp), Terracotta bull figurines, and Kosa silk handlooms.

states.name: Sikkim
states.overview: Nestled in the shadow of Mount Kangchenjunga (world’s 3rd highest peak), India’s first 100% organic state with historic Buddhist monasteries.
states.culture_desc: Cham sacred monastic mask dances, harmony between Lepcha, Bhutia, and Nepali ethnic heritages, and Buddhist prayer flags dotting mountain passes.
states.festivals_desc: Pang Lhabsol (honoring Mount Kangchenjunga), Losar (Tibetan New Year), Saga Dawa celebrating Buddha’s enlightenment, and Maghe Sankranti.
states.food_desc: Fermented Himalayan gastronomy: Steamed Momos, Thukpa soup, Gundruk fermented leafy greens, Kinema fermented soybeans, and Chhurpi hard cheese.
states.languages_desc: Nepali, Sikkimese (Bhutia), Lepcha, and English.
states.art_crafts_desc: Thangka religious scrolls, Choktse carved wooden folding tables, Lepcha traditional handlooms, and handmade bamboo paper.

states.name: Meghalaya
states.overview: The Abode of Clouds, home to Cherrapunji and Mawsynram (wettest places on Earth), indigenous bio-engineered Living Root Bridges, and matrilineal culture.
states.culture_desc: Matrilineal clan lineage where lineage passes through mothers, Nongkrem dance festival, and deep ecological reverence for Sacred Groves.
states.festivals_desc: Wangala 100-Drums harvest festival of the Garos, Shad Suk Mynsiem thanksgiving dance of the Khasis, and Shillong Cherry Blossom Festival.
states.food_desc: Khasi and Garo mountain cuisine: Jadoh red rice cooked with meat, Dohkhlieh pork and onion salad, Tungrymbai fermented beans, and Nakham fish stew.
states.languages_desc: Khasi, Garo, Pnar, and English (official).
states.art_crafts_desc: Cane and bamboo basketry, Tlieng woven grass mats, Endi silk handlooms, and traditional musical instruments (Duitara).

states.name: Arunachal Pradesh
states.overview: The Land of the Dawn-lit Mountains, first Indian land to greet the morning sun, home to 400-year-old Tawang Monastery and 26 major indigenous tribes.
states.culture_desc: Apatani sustainable bamboo forestry and facial tattoo heritage, Monpa Buddhist traditions, and Wancho woodcarvings.
states.festivals_desc: Losar Buddhist New Year, Ziro Music Festival in pine valley, Torgya monastic festival of Tawang, and Nyokum Yullo harvest celebration.
states.food_desc: Indigenous tribal flavors: Pika Pila fermented bamboo shoot pickle, Lukter dried beef with King Chilli, Dung Po steamed rice, and Apong rice beer.
states.languages_desc: English (official), Nyishi, Adi, Apatani, Monpa, and Hindi.
states.art_crafts_desc: Thangka painting, Monpa handmade Daphne paper, Wancho wood sculptures, Mishmi woven shawls, and cane bridge architecture.

states.name: Nagaland
states.overview: The Land of Festivals, rugged scenic hills, 16 distinct warrior tribes, historic Battle of Kohima memorial, and vibrant Hornbill cultural festival.
states.culture_desc: Morung youth dormitory institution, Angami warrior shawls with symbolic animal motifs, and oral epic folklore.
states.festivals_desc: Hornbill Festival at Kisama Heritage Village ("Festival of Festivals"), Moatsu Mong of Ao tribe, and Sekrenyi purification festival of Angamis.
states.food_desc: Fermented and smoked specialties: Smoked Pork with Axone (fermented soya), Anishi yam leaf cakes, King Chilli (Bhut Jolokia) chutneys, and Galho stew.
states.languages_desc: English (official), Nagamese creole, Ao, Angami, Lotha, and Sumi.
states.art_crafts_desc: Naga tribal warrior shawls (Tsungkotepsu), Handcrafted spear spears, Black pottery of Longkhim, and cane baskets.

states.name: Manipur
states.overview: The Jewel of India, birthplace of modern Polo (Sagol Kangjei), home to classical Manipuri Raas Leela dance and the floating Loktak Lake.
states.culture_desc: Classical Manipuri dance with hypnotic circular movements, Thang-Ta martial arts, Nata Sankirtana singing (UNESCO), and Meitei mythology.
states.festivals_desc: Yaoshang (spring festival featuring Thabal Chongba moonlight dance), Sangai Tourism Festival, Ningol Chakouba, and Cheiraoba New Year.
states.food_desc: Fresh, herb-forward Meitei cuisine: Kangshoi vegetable stew, Eromba fermented fish mash with King Chilli, Singju spicy salad, and Chak-hao black rice kheer.
states.languages_desc: Meiteilon (Manipuri, 8th Schedule language written in Meitei Mayek script).
states.art_crafts_desc: Kauna water reed handicrafts, Shaphee Lanphee ceremonial embroidered shawls, Longpi black stone pottery, and Wangkhei Phee fine muslin.

states.name: Mizoram
states.overview: The Land of the Hill People, dramatic misty peaks, high literacy, peaceful community ethics (Tlawmngaihna), and vibrant Cheraw bamboo dance.
states.culture_desc: Cheraw bamboo dance requiring rhythmic agility, community solidarity, Chheihlam folk dance, and rich choral singing heritage.
states.festivals_desc: Chapchar Kut post-jhum harvest celebration, Mim Kut maize festival, and Pawl Kut thanksgiving celebration.
states.food_desc: Delicate mountain cooking: Bai boiled vegetables with pork and bamboo shoot, Vawksa Rep smoked pork, Sawhchiar rice stew, and Sanpiau.
states.languages_desc: Mizo (official, written in Roman script) and English.
states.art_crafts_desc: Puan handwoven traditional shawls with geometric clan stripes, Cane baskets (Em), and bamboo furniture.

states.name: Tripura
states.overview: Ancient princely state celebrated for Ujjayanta Palace, Neermahal floating lake castle, and the colossal rock carvings of Unakoti.
states.culture_desc: Hojagiri balancing folk dance of the Reang tribe, Manikya dynasty royal heritage, and synthesis of Bengali and Tipra traditions.
states.festivals_desc: Kharchi Puja (worship of the 14 titular deities), Garia Puja tribal dance festival, and Neermahal Water Festival.
states.food_desc: Indigenous Tripuri cuisine: Mui Borok made with Berma (fermented fish), Chakwi alkaline bamboo shoot stew, and Chakhwi.
states.languages_desc: Bengali, Kokborok (native Sino-Tibetan language), and English.
states.art_crafts_desc: Bamboo and cane carvings, Rignai and Rikutu handlooms, and royal brass and bell-metal castings.

states.name: Delhi (NCT)
states.overview: Imperial capital through 8 historic cities, home to three UNESCO World Heritage Sites (Red Fort, Qutub Minar, Humayun’s Tomb) and vibrant street life.
states.culture_desc: Centuries of Mughal, Sultanate, and colonial fusion, Sufi Qawwalis of Hazrat Nizamuddin Dargah, and cosmopolitan cultural confluence.
states.festivals_desc: Phool Walon Ki Sair communal flower procession, Qutub Music Festival, India Gate Republic Day Parade, and Dilli Haat cultural melas.
states.food_desc: Legendary culinary epicenter: Chandni Chowk Parathas, Old Delhi Butter Chicken, Nihari, Chaat, Chole Bhature, and Daulat ki Chaat.
states.languages_desc: Hindi, English, Punjabi, and Urdu.
states.art_crafts_desc: Zari and Zardozi metallic embroidery, Blue Pottery of Delhi, and Meenakari enamel jewellery.

states.name: Chandigarh
states.overview: The City Beautiful, modern architectural masterpiece planned by Swiss-French architect Le Corbusier (UNESCO World Heritage Capitol Complex).
states.culture_desc: Urban green garden planning, contemporary art galleries, Rock Garden visionary sculpture park created from industrial waste by Nek Chand.
states.festivals_desc: Rose Festival at Zakir Hussain Rose Garden, Mango Festival, and Chandigarh Carnival.
states.food_desc: Punjabi and North Indian specialties: Chole Bhature, Tandoori Chicken, Kulcha, and Fresh Cane Juice.
states.languages_desc: English (official), Punjabi, and Hindi.
states.art_crafts_desc: Recycled stone and ceramic sculptures, Phulkari handlooms, and modernist terracotta pottery.

states.name: Puducherry
states.overview: The French Riviera of the East, famous for French colonial villas in White Town, Sri Aurobindo Ashram, and the universal township of Auroville.
states.culture_desc: Franco-Tamil architectural harmony, yoga and spiritual meditation retreats at Auroville Matrimandir, and classical Carnatic music.
states.festivals_desc: International Yoga Festival, French Bastille Day, Masi Magam sea-bath festival, and Auroville Golden Jubilee festivities.
states.food_desc: Franco-Tamil fusion cuisine: Bouillabaisse seafood stew, Baguettes, Ratatouille, Pondicherry Prawn Masala, and Crepes.
states.languages_desc: Tamil, French, Telugu, Malayalam, and English.
states.art_crafts_desc: Auroville handmade incense and organic skincare, Terracotta figurines, Handmade marbling paper, and leathercraft.

states.name: Andaman & Nicobar Islands
states.overview: Emerald tropical archipelago in the Bay of Bengal, home to the historic Cellular Jail (Kala Pani), pristine coral reefs, and ancient indigenous tribes.
states.culture_desc: Historic freedom fighter sacrifice at Cellular Jail, indigenous Jarawa, Sentinelese, and Nicobarese cultural heritage.
states.festivals_desc: Island Tourism Festival at Port Blair, Subhash Mela at Havelock, and Monsoon Music Festival.
states.food_desc: Fresh coastal sea catch: Grilled Lobster, Crab Masala, Fish Curry, Coconut Prawn Curry, and tropical fruits.
states.languages_desc: Hindi, English, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, and Nicobarese.
states.art_crafts_desc: Mother-of-pearl shell jewelry, Padauk timber woodwork, Cane and bamboo cane crafts, and coconut shell crafts.

states.name: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
states.hindi_name: दादरा और नगर हवेली एवं दमन और दीव
states.overview: Coastal western union territory featuring 16th-century Portuguese fortress walls, Nani Daman churches, golden beaches, and Warli tribal homelands.
states.culture_desc: Indo-Portuguese coastal heritage, Warli tribal art traditions, Tarpa folk dance, and Catholic feast processions.
states.festivals_desc: Nariyal Poornima (Coconut Day), Tarpa Dance Festival, Feast of Our Lady of Remedios, and Diu Festival.
states.food_desc: Coastal seafood and tribal cuisine: Dhonslo steamed cake, Fish Koliwada, Prawn Balchao, and Ubadiyu smoked winter greens.
states.languages_desc: Gujarati, Hindi, Marathi, and Portuguese creole.
states.art_crafts_desc: Warli bamboo paintings, Mat weaving, Tortoise shell handicrafts, and handcrafted fishing boats.

states.name: Lakshadweep
states.overview: Group of 36 serene coral atolls in the Arabian Sea, crystalline turquoise lagoons, coconut groves, and rich maritime Islamic heritage.
states.culture_desc: Kolkali and Parichakali martial shield dances, boat building, and centuries-old sea trade ties with the Malabar coast.
states.festivals_desc: Eid-ul-Fitr, Eid-ul-Adha, Milad-un-Nabi, and Muharram celebrated with traditional music and community boat regattas.
states.food_desc: Tuna and coconut-forward cuisine: Masmin (sun-dried smoked tuna), Ray Mus Kavaab, Batla Appam, and Coconut Rice.
states.languages_desc: Jesyri (dialect of Malayalam), Mahl (in Minicoy), and English.
states.art_crafts_desc: Coir twisting and carpet weaving, Coral and seashell art, Coconut shell carvings, and miniature wooden boats.

categories.description: Hilltop fortresses, desert citadels, defensive ramparts, and royal courts.

categories.description: Intricate handicrafts, ancient block printing, miniature paintings, and bronze casting.

categories.name: Festivals & Performing Arts
categories.description: Classical dance forms, temple rituals, musical traditions, and fairs.

categories.name: Culinary Heritage
categories.description: Time-honored royal recipes, regional thalis, and Ayurvedic spiced delicacies.

heritage.title: Taj Mahal (Crown of the Palace)
heritage.summary: An ivory-white marble mausoleum on the south bank of the Yamuna River, universally acknowledged as the jewel of Muslim art in India.
heritage.history: Commissioned in 1631 by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan to house the tomb of his favourite wife, Mumtaz Mahal; completed around 1648.
heritage.culture: Combines Persian, Islamic, and Indian architectural traditions. Features pristine Pietra Dura gemstone inlay work and symmetrical gardens symbolizing paradise (Charbagh).

heritage.title: Qutub Minar & Iron Pillar Complex
heritage.summary: The tallest brick minaret in the world (72.5 m), alongside the 1,600-year-old rust-resistant metallurgical marvel of the Gupta Iron Pillar.
heritage.history: Construction started in 1192 by Qutb-ud-din Aibak and expanded by Iltutmish and Firoz Shah Tughlaq in the Delhi Sultanate era.
heritage.culture: Showcases the synthesis of Indo-Islamic calligraphy, fluted sandstone balconies, and the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque colonnade.

heritage.title: Red Fort (Lal Qila)
heritage.summary: UNESCO World Heritage red sandstone citadel that served as the primary residence of the Mughal emperors for nearly 200 years.
heritage.history: Commissioned by Emperor Shah Jahan in 1638 when he shifted the imperial capital from Agra to Shahjahanabad; completed in 1648.
heritage.culture: Venue for the Prime Minister’s Independence Day address from the Lahori Gate ramparts. Houses Diwan-i-Aam and Diwan-i-Khas.

heritage.title: India Gate & Kartavya Path
heritage.summary: Monumental 42-metre war arch honoring 84,000 soldiers of the British Indian Army who died in World War I and the Third Anglo-Afghan War.
heritage.history: Designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens and completed in 1931; recently unified with the National War Memorial along the revamped Kartavya Path.
heritage.culture: The Amar Jawan Jyoti and the grand canopy commemorating Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose make it a civic emblem of valor.
heritage.timings: Open 24 hours (Illuminated in Tricolour after dusk)

heritage.title: Amber Palace & Fort
heritage.summary: Magnificent Rajput stronghold overlooking Maota Lake, famous for its artistic Hindu elements, massive ramparts, and Sheesh Mahal mirror palace.
heritage.history: Constructed originally by Raja Man Singh I in 1592 CE on the ruins of an older structure, Amber was the fortified residence of the Kachwaha clan until Sawai Jai Singh II founded Jaipur in 1727.
heritage.culture: Blends Rajput and Mughal architectural aesthetics. Famous for the Diwan-i-Aam (Hall of Public Audience), Sheesh Mahal (Hall of Mirrors illuminated by a single candle flame), and Sukh Niwas with an evaporative cooling system.
heritage.timings: 08:00 AM - 05:30 PM, Evening Light & Sound Show: 06:30 PM

heritage.title: Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds)
heritage.summary: Five-storey honeycomb facade constructed of red and pink sandstone with 953 intricately carved jharokha casements.
heritage.history: Built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh and designed by Lal Chand Ustad, modeled after the crown of Lord Krishna.
heritage.culture: Allowed royal women to observe festive street processions in the Johari Bazaar while preserving the strict Purdah custom.

heritage.title: Gateway of India
heritage.summary: Colossal basalt arch monument rising 85 feet over Mumbai Harbor, combining Indo-Islamic 16th-century Gujarati design elements.
heritage.history: Erected to commemorate the 1911 landing of King George V and Queen Mary. Witnessed the ceremonial departure of the last British troops in 1948.
heritage.culture: Mumbai’s civic landmark overlooking the Arabian Sea, serving as the ferry departure terminal to Elephanta Island caves.

heritage.title: Sri Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple)
heritage.summary: The spiritual and cultural epicentre of Sikhism, coated in pure gold foil and surrounded by the sacred Amrit Sarovar (Pool of Nectar).
heritage.history: Founded in 1577 by Guru Ram Das Ji; the sanctum foundation was laid by Sufi saint Hazrat Mian Mir, and gold plating was gifted by Maharaja Ranjit Singh.
heritage.culture: Open to people of all faiths through four welcoming entrances. Runs the world’s largest community kitchen (Guru ka Langar) serving over 100,000 daily meals.

heritage.title: Ajanta & Ellora Rock-Cut Caves
heritage.summary: Monumental rock-hewn caves including the Kailasa Temple (Cave 16), the world’s largest single monolithic rock excavation on Earth.
heritage.history: Ajanta caves carved between 2nd century BCE and 5th century CE; Ellora sanctuaries excavated between 6th and 10th centuries CE under Rashtrakuta and Yadava patronages.
heritage.culture: Ellora harmoniously unites Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain sanctuaries side by side. Kailasa temple was carved vertically top-down out of basalt cliff without scaffolding.
heritage.timings: 09:00 AM - 05:00 PM (Ajanta closed Mondays, Ellora closed Tuesdays)

heritage.title: Sun Temple of Konark (Black Pagoda)
heritage.summary: UNESCO World Heritage 13th-century architectural marvel designed as a colossal 24-wheeled chariot pulled by seven straining stone horses.
heritage.history: Constructed around 1250 CE by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty using khondalite rocks on the Bay of Bengal shore.
heritage.culture: The 24 intricately carved stone wheels function as precise sundials showing time down to the minute via sunbeam shadows.
heritage.timings: 06:00 AM - 08:00 PM (Light & Sound show at 07:00 PM)
heritage.best_time: October to March (Konark Dance Festival in December)

heritage.title: Group of Monuments at Hampi
heritage.summary: UNESCO World Heritage capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, sprawling over 4,100 hectares of surreal boulder-strewn terrain on the Tungabhadra River.
heritage.history: Flourished in the 14th to 16th centuries as one of the world’s largest and richest cities, admired by Portuguese travelers Duarte Barbosa and Domingo Paes.
heritage.culture: Famed for the iconic Stone Chariot at the Vijaya Vittala Temple with musical pillars that emit musical swaras when tapped.
heritage.best_time: October to March (Hampi Utsav in November/January)

heritage.title: Great Stupa at Sanchi
heritage.summary: One of India's oldest stone structures, a hemispherical Buddhist dome enshrining relics of the Buddha, surrounded by intricately carved Toranas.
heritage.history: Originally commissioned by Mauryan Emperor Ashoka the Great in the 3rd century BCE, and expanded under Sunga and Satavahana rulers.
heritage.culture: The four ornate gateways (Toranas) narrate Jataka tales, Buddhist miracles, and ancient Indian flora and fauna in high relief.

heritage.title: Victoria Memorial Hall
heritage.summary: Grand Makrana marble palace surrounded by 64 acres of gardens, blending British and Mughal architectural traditions.
heritage.history: Conceived by Lord Curzon after Queen Victoria’s death in 1901; inaugurated in 1921. Built of the same white marble quarry as the Taj Mahal.
heritage.culture: Preserves rare oil paintings by Thomas and William Daniell, royal manuscripts, and a 16-foot bronze Angel of Victory rotating on ball bearings.
heritage.timings: Gardens: 05:30 AM - 06:15 PM, Museum: 10:00 AM - 05:00 PM (Closed Mondays)
heritage.location_name: Queens Way, Maidan, Kolkata, West Bengal

heritage.title: Charminar & Laad Bazaar
heritage.summary: The iconic 1591 AD ceremonial monument and mosque featuring four 56-metre minarets rising over Hyderabad’s pearl and lac-bangle street market.
heritage.history: Commissioned by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, the fifth sultan of the Qutb Shahi dynasty, to commemorate the end of a deadly plague in the city.
heritage.culture: Surrounded by historic Irani chai cafes, Osmania biscuit bakeries, and the vibrant scent of Ittar perfumes in the shadow of Mecca Masjid.
heritage.timings: 09:00 AM - 05:30 PM (Lit in gold at night)

heritage.title: Golconda Fort (The Diamond Citadel)
heritage.summary: Colossal fortified medieval fortress famed for its acoustic sound engineering, where a handclap at the entrance can be heard 1 km away atop Bala Hissar.
heritage.history: Original mud fort built by the Kakatiyas, expanded into an impenetrable granite citadel by the Qutb Shahi kings; source of Koh-i-Noor and Hope diamonds.
heritage.culture: Features 87 semi-circular bastions, cannon-mounted battlements (Fateh Rahben), and a subterranean acoustic security warning system.
heritage.timings: 09:00 AM - 05:30 PM (Sound & Light show at 06:30 PM)

heritage.title: Mahabodhi Temple Complex (Bodh Gaya)
heritage.summary: UNESCO World Heritage sacred 50-metre pyramidal brick temple marking the exact spot where Prince Siddhartha attained supreme Enlightenment.
heritage.history: First temple built by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE; present grand brick structure dates from the 5th–6th century Gupta period.
heritage.culture: Houses the sacred Bodhi Tree (direct descendant of original tree), the Diamond Throne (Vajrasana), and the Animesh Lochan Chaitya.
heritage.best_time: October to March (Buddha Jayanti in May)

heritage.title: Brihadisvara Temple (Peruvudaiyar Kovil)
heritage.summary: Monumental 11th-century Chola granite temple topped by an 80-tonne monolithic cupola that casts no midday shadow at the equinox.
heritage.history: Commissioned by Emperor Rajaraja Chola I and consecrated in 1010 CE to celebrate his maritime conquests across the Indian Ocean.
heritage.culture: A masterpiece of Dravidian architecture entirely constructed of granite transported without wheels from 50 miles away. Features India’s second-largest monolithic Nandi bull.

heritage.title: Mysore Palace (Amba Vilas)
heritage.summary: Spectacular three-storey Indo-Saracenic royal seat of the Wadiyar dynasty, illuminated by 97,000 electric bulbs during Sunday dusk and Dasara.
heritage.history: Designed by British royal architect Henry Irwin and completed in 1912 after the old wooden palace was destroyed by fire in 1897.
heritage.culture: Hosts the world-famous Mysore Dasara procession where the idol of Goddess Chamundeshwari is carried on a 750-kg golden Howdah atop an elephant.
heritage.timings: 10:00 AM - 05:30 PM (Illumination on Sundays & holidays: 07:00 PM - 07:45 PM)
heritage.best_time: October to March (Mysore Dasara in September/October)

heritage.title: Mehrangarh Fort
heritage.summary: One of India’s grandest citadels, towering 400 feet above the Sun City of Jodhpur with impregnable walls and palatial courtyards.
heritage.history: Founded in 1459 by Rao Jodha, 15th Rathore ruler, when he moved his capital from Mandore to the rocky ridge known as Bhakurcheeria.
heritage.culture: Houses world-class museum galleries exhibiting royal palanquins (howdahs), Marwar miniature paintings, armory, and preserved chambers like the Phool Mahal and Sheesh Mahal.

heritage.title: Jaisalmer Golden Fort (Sonar Qila)
heritage.summary: The living golden sandstone fortress rising like a mirage from the Thar Desert sands, sheltering a vibrant quarter of the city within its gates.
heritage.history: Erected in 1156 CE by the Rajput ruler Rawal Jaisal. Positioned strategically on the ancient Silk Route connecting India to Persia and Egypt.
heritage.culture: One of the few fully inhabited forts in the world. Encloses seven ornate yellow sandstone Jain temples built between the 12th and 16th centuries.

heritage.title: Chittorgarh Fort & Vijay Stambha
heritage.summary: The largest fort complex in India, immortalized in ballads for Rajput valor, Rani Padmini, and the majestic 9-story Tower of Victory.
heritage.history: Seat of the Guhila and Sisodia rulers of Mewar from the 7th to 16th centuries. Witnessed epic sieges by Alauddin Khalji and Emperor Akbar.
heritage.culture: Features Vijay Stambha (Tower of Victory built by Maharana Kumbha in 1448) and Kirti Stambha, along with historic water reservoirs that held up to 4 billion liters of water.

heritage.title: Humayun’s Tomb (Maqbara-e-Humayun)
heritage.summary: The first grand garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent, hailed as the architectural inspiration for the Taj Mahal.
heritage.history: Commissioned in 1558 by Humayun’s senior consort Bega Begum and designed by Persian master architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyas.
heritage.culture: Exemplifies the quadripartite Charbagh paradise garden layout with causeways, flowing water channels, and red-white marble geometry.

heritage.title: Parasnath Hill & Shikharji
heritage.summary: The most sacred pilgrimage shrine of Jainism rising 4,430 feet, where twenty of the twenty-four Tirthankaras attained Moksha (liberation).
heritage.history:
History & Origin
Origin: Parasnath Hill is named after Lord Parshvanatha, the 23rd Jain Tirthankara.
Ancient Name: The hill is traditionally known as Sammed Shikhar, one of Jainism’s most sacred pilgrimage sites.
Religious History: 20 of the 24 Jain Tirthankaras are believed to have attained salvation here.
Ancient Heritage: The site has been associated with Jain pilgrimage since ancient times, with some temples traditionally believed to be over 2,000 years old.
heritage.culture: Devotees complete a sacred 27 km circumambulation (Parikrama) barefoot visiting the footprints (Charan Paduka) of liberated souls.

heritage.title: Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple
heritage.summary: Ancient temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu in Anantha Shayana posture, renowned for Chera-Dravidian architecture and sacred underground vaults.
heritage.history: Mentioned in Sangam literature and the Tamil Divya Prabandham (6th–9th centuries CE). Extensively refurbished in the 18th century by King Marthanda Varma of Travancore.
heritage.culture: Adheres to strict Vedic dress codes and traditional Kerala rituals. Features a 100-foot seven-tier gopuram beside the sacred Padma Theertham tank.
heritage.timings: 03:30 AM - 12:00 PM, 05:00 PM - 08:30 PM (Dress code mandatory)

heritage.title: Shri Somnath Jyotirlinga Temple
heritage.summary: The first and foremost of the twelve sacred Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva, standing proudly on the coast of the Arabian Sea.
heritage.history: Known as "The Shrine Eternal", reconstructed repeatedly across centuries, with the present majestic Kailash Mahameru Prasad completed in 1951.
heritage.culture: The Arrow Pillar (Baan Stambh) marks an unobstructed sea route from Somnath all the way to Antarctica along the meridian.

heritage.title: Statue of Unity (Sardar Patel)
heritage.summary: The world's tallest statue (182 metres) honoring Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, overlooking the scenic Narmada River and Sardar Sarovar Dam.
heritage.history: Inaugurated on 31 October 2018 to commemorate the Iron Man of India who unified 562 princely states into the Indian Union.
heritage.culture: Engineered by Padma Bhushan sculptor Ram V. Sutar, symbolizing national solidarity and sustainable tribal development in the Kevadia valley.

heritage.title: Rani ki Vav (The Queen’s Stepwell)
heritage.summary: An intricate seven-storey subterranean stepwell on the banks of the Saraswati River, constructed in the distinctive Maru-Gurjara style.
heritage.history: Built in 1063 AD by Queen Udayamati in memory of Chaulukya King Bhima I. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014.
heritage.culture: Features over 500 principal sculptures and 1,000 minor carved panels honoring Lord Vishnu’s ten avatars (Dashavatara).

heritage.title: Maa Kamakhya Devalaya (Nilachal Hill)
heritage.summary: The most venerable of the 51 Shakti Peethas celebrating womanhood and creation, where the Yoni of Goddess Sati fell.
heritage.history: Dates to ancient Tantric traditions; the present distinctive beehive-domed Nilachal temple was rebuilt in 1565 by Koch King Naranarayan.
heritage.culture: Focal point of the annual Ambubachi Mela, during which the Brahmaputra River runs sacred red symbolizing the earth’s fertility.
heritage.best_time: October to April (Ambubachi Mela in June)

heritage.title: Shree Jagannath Temple (Puri Dham)
heritage.summary: Sacred Char Dham pilgrimage shrine rising 214 feet high, world-famous for the grand annual Rath Yatra chariot procession.
heritage.history: Built in the 12th century by King Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva, enshrining Lord Jagannath, Balabhadra, and Subhadra carved from sacred Neem wood.
heritage.culture: Features the world’s largest traditional kitchen (Ananda Bazar) preparing Mahaprasad cooked in 7 earthen pots stacked over single wood fires.
heritage.best_time: October to March (Rath Yatra in June/July)

heritage.title: Varanasi Ghats & Kashi Vishwanath
heritage.hindi_title: वाराणसी के घाट एवं काशी विश्वनाथ
heritage.summary: Ancient continuous spiritual civilization along the crescent curve of Mother Ganga, known for Dashashwamedh Aarti and sacred cremation ghats.
heritage.history: Inhabited continuously for over 3,000 years, praised by Mark Twain as "older than history, older than tradition, older even than legend".
heritage.culture: Witness to the soul of Sanatana Dharma. Features 84 historic stone stepped ghats, early morning boat rides, and the newly renovated Kashi Vishwanath Dham corridor.
heritage.timings: Open 24 hours, Evening Ganga Aarti: 06:45 PM

heritage.title: Fatehpur Sikri & Buland Darwaza
heritage.summary: Emperor Akbar’s red sandstone utopian capital, featuring the 54-meter Buland Darwaza and the marble tomb of Sufi saint Sheikh Salim Chishti.
heritage.history: Founded in 1571 CE by Akbar as the capital of the Mughal Empire; abandoned in 1585 due to scarcity of fresh drinking water.
heritage.culture: A synthesis of regional Gujarati, Rajasthani, and Persian design idioms, including the legendary Panch Mahal five-story pavilion and Diwan-i-Khas central pillar.
heritage.location_name: Fatehpur Sikri, Agra District, Uttar Pradesh

heritage.title: Elephanta Caves (Gharapuri)
heritage.summary: Rock-cut cave temples situated on an island in Mumbai Harbor, featuring the sublime 20-foot Sadashiva Trimurti sculpture of Lord Shiva.
heritage.history: Carved between the 5th and 8th centuries CE under Konkan Maurya and Rashtrakuta dynasties.
heritage.culture: Celebrated for the Trimurti depicting Shiva as Creator (Vamadeva), Preserver (Tatpurusha), and Destroyer (Aghora Bhairava).

heritage.title: Monuments of Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram)
heritage.summary: Ancient Pallava seaside sanctuaries including the Shore Temple, Pancha Rathas monolithic rock-cut shrines, and Arjuna’s Penance relief.
heritage.history: Carved during the 7th and 8th centuries CE under Pallava kings Mahendravarman I and Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla).
heritage.culture: Arjuna’s Penance (Descent of the Ganges) is one of the world’s largest open-air stone bas-reliefs, depicting gods, celestial nymphs, and wildlife.

heritage.title: Cellular Jail National Memorial (Kala Pani)
heritage.summary: Historic colonial panopticon prison where Veer Savarkar, Batukeshwar Dutt, and Indian freedom fighters endured solitary confinement.
heritage.history: Built by the British between 1896 and 1906 with seven radiating brick wings containing 693 individual solitary cells designed to prevent prisoner communication.
heritage.culture: Now a sacred national shrine holding the eternal flame (Swatantrya Jyot) and hosting an evocative evening Light and Sound show narrated by an ancient Peepal tree.
heritage.timings: 09:00 AM - 12:30 PM, 01:30 PM - 04:45 PM (Sound & Light show at 06:00 PM, closed Mondays)

heritage.title: Howrah Bridge (Rabindra Setu)
heritage.summary: Pioneering balanced cantilever bridge spanning 1,500 feet over the Hooghly River without a single pylon in the riverbed.
heritage.history: Commissioned in 1943 during World War II using 26,500 tonnes of high-tensile alloy steel supplied by Tata Steel.
heritage.culture: The iconic gateway to the City of Joy, carrying over 100,000 vehicles and 150,000 pedestrians every day.
heritage.timings: Open 24 hours (Best viewed illuminated at dusk)

heritage.title: Ancient Nalanda Mahavihara University
heritage.summary: UNESCO World Heritage archaeological ruins of the ancient world’s greatest residential university, welcoming 10,000 students and 2,000 scholars.
heritage.history: Flourished from the 5th to 12th century CE under the Gupta and Pala empires; visited by Chinese pilgrims Xuanzang and Yijing.
heritage.culture: Center of Buddhist philosophy, astronomy, medicine, and mathematics. Features the iconic votive stupas of Sariputta and meditation viharas.

heritage.title: Badrinath Temple (Badri Vishal)
heritage.summary: One of the holy Char Dham and Chota Char Dham pilgrimage shrines dedicated to Lord Vishnu, located on the banks of the Alaknanda River.
heritage.history: Established in Vedic antiquity and consecrated as a major pilgrimage center by Adi Shankaracharya in the 9th century.
heritage.culture: Famed for its bright conical arched facade, Tapt Kund thermal sulfur springs, and Neelkanth peak forming a snowy backdrop.
heritage.best_time: May to June, September to October

heritage.title: Agra Fort (Lal Qila)
heritage.summary: The main imperial residence of the Mughal emperors until 1638, constructed with striking red sandstone ramparts over 2.5 kilometers long.
heritage.history: Rebuilt by Emperor Akbar from an older brick citadel named Badalgarh. Shah Jahan later embellished it with white marble pavilions.
heritage.culture: Contains the Khas Mahal, Diwan-i-Aam, Jahangir Mahal, and the Musamman Burj balcony where Shah Jahan spent his final years gazing across the river at the Taj Mahal.

heritage.title: Jantar Mantar Astronomical Observatory
heritage.summary: A collection of nineteen monumental architectural astronomical instruments, including the world’s largest stone sundial.
heritage.history: Built by Rajput king Sawai Jai Singh II between 1728 and 1734 to compile astronomical tables and predict movements of celestial bodies.
heritage.culture: Represented peak astronomical science in 18th-century Asia, blending Ptolemaic and Hindu Vedic calculations with monumental stone masonry.
heritage.best_time: Year-round, best at midday when sun is overhead

heritage.title: Sun Temple of Modhera
heritage.summary: Magnificent 11th-century temple complex dedicated to the solar deity Surya, designed so that equinox sunbeams illuminate the sanctum.
heritage.history: Built in 1026–27 AD during the reign of King Bhima I of the Chaulukya dynasty beside the holy river Pushpavati.
heritage.culture: Comprises the Sabha Mandapa (Assembly Hall), Guda Mandapa (Sanctum), and the stepped Surya Kund with 108 miniature shrines.
heritage.best_time: October to March (Modhera Dance Festival in January)

heritage.title: Gwalior Fort (Gibraltar of India)
heritage.summary: Impregnable 8th-century hill citadel rising 300 feet above Gwalior city, famed for turquoise enameled tile mosaics and the Man Mandir Palace.
heritage.history: Ruled successively by Tomar Rajputs, Mughals, Marathas, and Scindias; praised by Mughal Emperor Babur as "the pearl among fortresses of Hind".
heritage.culture: Houses the Teli ka Mandir, Sas Bahu Temples, and colossal rock-cut Jain Tirthankara colossi carved directly into the cliff walls.

heritage.title: Kakatiya Rudreshwara (Ramappa) Temple
heritage.summary: UNESCO World Heritage 800-year-old temple built of buoyant "floating bricks" that are lighter than water, perched on a 6-foot star-shaped platform.
heritage.history: Erected in 1213 CE by Kakatiya General Recharla Rudra during the reign of Ganapati Deva, named uniquely after its chief sculptor, Ramappa.
heritage.culture: Adorned with black basalt bracket figures depicting graceful bracket dancers (Madanikas) praised by traveler Marco Polo as "the brightest star in the galaxy of temples".

heritage.title: Lepakshi Veerabhadra & The Hanging Pillar
heritage.hindi_title: लेपाक्षी वीरभद्र मंदिर एवं झूलता खंभा
heritage.summary: 16th-century Vijayanagara temple marvel famous for its miraculous Hanging Pillar that doesn’t touch the ground, and India’s largest monolithic Nandi.
heritage.history: Constructed around 1530 AD by merchant brothers Virupanna and Veeranna, governors under Vijayanagara Emperor Achyuta Deva Raya.
heritage.culture: Holds the largest ceiling fresco in Asia depicting Lord Shiva’s wedding, and a 38-foot colossal granite Nandi bull 200 metres from the temple.
heritage.location_name: Sri Sathya Sai District, Andhra Pradesh

heritage.title: Sundarbans Biosphere & Heritage
heritage.summary: The largest mangrove forest in the world, formed at the confluence of the Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers, home of the Royal Bengal Tiger.
heritage.history: Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1987 for its extraordinary ecological and tidal delta processes.
heritage.culture: Rich folklore celebrating Bonbibi (Guardian Spirit of the Forests) venerated equally by Hindu and Muslim honey collectors and fishermen.

heritage.title: Tawang Monastery (Galden Namgey Lhatse)
heritage.hindi_title: तवांग मठ (भारत का सबसे बड़ा मठ)
heritage.summary: The largest Buddhist monastery in India and second largest in the world, fortified like a fortress on a cliff at 10,000 feet near the Bhutanese border.
heritage.history: Founded in 1680–81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyamtso in accordance with the wishes of the 5th Dalai Lama.
heritage.culture: Enshrines an 28-foot gilded Buddha in the Dukhang assembly hall, holding 400-year-old gold-lettered Buddhist Kangyur and Tengyur scriptures.
heritage.best_time: March to October (Torgya Festival in January)

heritage.title: Nongriat Double Decker Living Root Bridge
heritage.hindi_title: नोंगरियाट डबल डेकर लिविंग रूट ब्रिज
heritage.summary: Miraculous bio-engineering living bridges grown by the indigenous Khasi tribe by guiding aerial roots of Ficus elastica fig trees across roaring jungle streams.
heritage.history: Passed down across centuries through traditional ecological knowledge; roots grow stronger with age and can support 50 people simultaneously.
heritage.culture: Recognized on the tentative UNESCO list as a global model of harmonious human-nature architecture and sacred grove conservation.
heritage.timings: Daylight hours (Trek of 3,500 stone steps down from Tyrna)

heritage.title: Rumtek Monastery (Dharma Chakra Centre)
heritage.summary: The grandest monastery in Sikkim, serving as the international seat of His Holiness the Gyalwang Karmapa of the Karma Kagyu order.
heritage.history: Originally built in the 1730s by the 9th Karmapa, and rebuilt as a majestic Tibetan architectural complex in 1966.
heritage.culture: Houses golden stupas containing relics of the 16th Karmapa, sacred murals, 1,001 miniature golden Buddhas, and Tibetan silk thangkas.
heritage.best_time: March to May, October to December

heritage.title: Loktak Lake & Floating Phumdis
heritage.summary: The largest natural freshwater lake in Northeast India, featuring unique floating circular biomass islands known as Phumdis.
heritage.history: Houses Keibul Lamjao, the world’s only floating national park, and the last natural refuge of the endangered Sangai brow-antlered dancing deer.
heritage.culture: Fisherfolk live in traditional huts atop these floating islands, weaving bamboo nets and harvesting edible lotus roots and water lilies.

heritage.title: Reiek Heritage Model Village
heritage.summary: A preserved hilltop traditional Mizo village showcasing authentic chieftain houses, bachelor quarters (Zawlbuk), and weapon vaults.
heritage.history: Maintained to preserve the egalitarian community code of "Tlawmngaihna" (selfless service to others) before colonial modernization.
heritage.culture: Perched below the dramatic Reiek Cliff with panoramic views across hills stretching towards the Chittagong Hill Tracts.
heritage.best_time: October to April (Anthourium Festival in September/October)

heritage.title: Kisama Naga Heritage Village
heritage.summary: A living cultural amphitheatre preserving authentic traditional Morungs (dormitories) representing all 17 recognized indigenous tribes of Nagaland.
heritage.history: Constructed by the Government of Nagaland to host the international Hornbill Festival ("Festival of Festivals") celebrated every December.
heritage.culture: Each tribal Morung displays unique woodcarvings, war drums, hornbill feather headdresses, tribal spears, and stone monoliths.

heritage.title: Dakshineswar Kali Temple
heritage.summary: Navaratna (nine-spire) temple on the eastern bank of the Hooghly, consecrated in 1855 and sanctified by mystic Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa.
heritage.history: Founded by philanthropist Rani Rashmoni, a pioneering woman who defied orthodox social barriers to build this egalitarian shrine.
heritage.culture: Features the presiding deity Bhavatarini, surrounded by 12 identical Shiva shrines along the riverfront.

heritage.title: Santiniketan (Abode of Peace)
heritage.summary: Universalist residential school and centre of art founded by Nobel Laureate Rabindranath Tagore, inscribed on the UNESCO list in 2023.
heritage.history: Established in 1901 by Rabindranath Tagore to offer an open-air education rooted in Indian classical values and nature.
heritage.culture: Birthplace of the Bengal School of Art with pioneers Nandalal Bose, Ramkinkar Baij, and Benode Behari Mukherjee.
heritage.best_time: November to February (Poush Mela in late December)

heritage.title: Terracotta Temples of Bishnupur
heritage.summary: Exquisite 17th-century terracotta temples built by Malla kings using carved burnt clay tiles depicting scenes from Hindu epics.
heritage.history: Patronized by Malla ruler Bir Hambir and successors who converted to Gaudiya Vaishnavism and made Bishnupur a cultural center.
heritage.culture: Showcases Bengal Chala architecture (curved eaved roofs imitating bamboo huts) such as the Rasmancha, Jor Bangla, and Shyam Rai temple.

heritage.title: Bara Imambara & Bhool Bhulaiya
heritage.summary: Nawabi architectural triumph in Lucknow featuring the world’s largest unsupported arched hall and an intricate three-dimensional labyrinth.
heritage.history: Built in 1784 by Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula as a humanitarian famine relief project to provide employment during devastating drought years.
heritage.culture: Engineered entirely without iron beams or wooden girders using interlocking Lakhori brick masonry and rice-husk mortar.

heritage.title: Sarnath & Dhamek Stupa
heritage.summary: The deer park where Gautama Buddha delivered his first sermon (Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta) and set the Wheel of Law in motion.
heritage.history: Erected in 500 CE over an earlier Mauryan structure commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in 249 BCE. Origin site of India’s National Emblem (Lion Capital).
heritage.culture: Sacred Buddhist pilgrimage destination with monastic ruins, Ashoka Pillar edicts, and the Mulagandha Kuti Vihara.

heritage.title: Mattancherry Dutch Palace
heritage.summary: Royal palace gifted by the Portuguese in 1555 CE, featuring Kerala Nalukettu timber architecture and vibrant Ramayana mural paintings.
heritage.history: Built around 1555 by the Portuguese as a goodwill gift to King Veera Kerala Varma of Cochin, later renovated by the Dutch in 1663.
heritage.culture: Its walls preserve tempera murals depicting episodes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Krishna Lila in classical Kerala pictorial style.

heritage.title: Bekal Fort & Keyhole Bastion
heritage.summary: Largest sea-facing citadel in Kerala, sweeping along the Arabian Sea with observation towers and subterranean tunnels.
heritage.history: Built by Shivappa Nayaka of Keladi in 1650 CE, later held by Tipu Sultan and utilized as an important defense post.
heritage.culture: Unlike residential palaces, Bekal was purely military, designed with zig-zag entrances, firing slits aimed at naval invaders, and a water-tank observation post.

heritage.title: Ramanathaswamy Temple Rameswaram
heritage.summary: Sacred Char Dham coastal temple boasting the longest pillared corridor in the world, with over 1,200 carved sandstone pillars.
heritage.history: Built during the 12th century by Pandya dynasty rulers and patronized by Jaffna kingdom kings and Sethupathi chieftains.
heritage.culture: One of the twelve sacred Jyotirlingas. Pilgrims take holy baths in 22 sacred Theerthams (wells) within temple premises.

heritage.title: Nilgiri Mountain Railway (Toy Train)
heritage.summary: Historic 1,000 mm meter gauge rack railway winding through the Blue Mountains using the alternate biting teeth Abt system.
heritage.history: Completed in 1908 by the British South Indian Railway, conquering steep gradients through 16 tunnels and 250 bridges.
heritage.culture: Part of the UNESCO Mountain Railways of India, powered by vintage steam locomotives through tea estates and misty shola forests.

heritage.title: Gangaikonda Cholapuram Temple
heritage.summary: The City of the Chola who conquered the Ganges, built with concave graceful curves to honor maritime empire victories.
heritage.history: Built in 1035 CE by Rajendra Chola I after his military expedition reached the River Ganga and brought back holy water.
heritage.culture: Forms part of the Great Living Chola Temples UNESCO World Heritage site, famous for sculptural bronzes of Nataraja and Ardhanarishvara.

heritage.title: Nek Chand’s Rock Garden
heritage.summary: Visionary 40-acre sculpture wonderland constructed entirely from industrial, urban, and domestic ceramic waste and river boulders.
heritage.history: Created secretly by government road inspector Nek Chand Saini starting in 1957, now celebrated worldwide as an outsider art masterpiece.
heritage.culture: Features winding courtyards, stone amphitheaters, cascading waterfalls, and thousands of sculptures made of broken glass bangles and pottery.

heritage.title: The Capitol Complex (Le Corbusier)
heritage.summary: UNESCO World Heritage modernist government complex designed by legendary Swiss-French master architect Le Corbusier.
heritage.history: Conceived in the 1950s as a symbol of newly independent India, inscribed on the UNESCO list in 2016.
heritage.culture: Comprises the monumental Secretariat, Legislative Assembly, High Court, and the iconic 28-metre rotating Open Hand Monument.

heritage.title: Tomb of Sheikh Chilli (Taj of Haryana)
heritage.hindi_title: शेख़ चिल्ली का मक़बरा (हरियाणा का ताज)
heritage.summary: A resplendent octagonal pearly marble mausoleum dedicated to Sufi Saint Abd-ur-Rahim, mentor to Mughal prince Dara Shikoh.
heritage.history: Constructed in the 17th century atop a high archaeological mound amidst sprawling Mughal gardens and an adjoining medieval madrasa.
heritage.culture: Features floral Pietra Dura stone inlays, vaulted arcades, and a central garden tank echoing classic Shah Jahani balance.

heritage.title: Sukhna Lake Heritage Promenade
heritage.summary: Iconic 3-sq-km rainfed reservoir and wetland created at the foothills of the Shivaliks, designed as a peaceful sanctuary for Chandigarh citizens.
heritage.history: Created in 1958 by Le Corbusier and chief engineer P.L. Verma by damming the seasonal Sukhna Choe stream.
heritage.culture: Declared an eco-sensitive zone hosting winter migratory Siberian ducks, heritage solar boats, and morning walking trails.

heritage.title: Gol Gumbaz (The Whispering Gallery)
heritage.summary: The mausoleum of Mohammed Adil Shah, featuring the second largest dome in the world (44 m diameter) constructed without pillar support.
heritage.history: Completed in 1656 by architect Yaqut of Dabul after 30 years of construction under the Adil Shahi dynasty of Bijapur.
heritage.culture: Its famous Whispering Gallery echoes even the faintest whisper 7 to 11 times distinctly across the immense circular expanse.

heritage.title: Lingaraja Temple Complex
heritage.summary: The pinnacle of Kalinga temple architecture, a towering 180-foot deula spire presiding over the temple city of Bhubaneswar.
heritage.history: Built in the 11th century by Somavamsi King Jajati Keshari and consecrated to Lord Harihara, a unified form of Shiva and Vishnu.
heritage.culture: Surrounded by 150 subsidiary shrines and the sacred Bindusagar tank containing waters gathered from all holy rivers of India.

heritage.title: Baba Baidyanath Jyotirlinga Dham
heritage.summary: One of the twelve sacred Jyotirlingas, revered as Kamna Linga where Ravana sacrificed ten heads in devotion to Lord Shiva.
heritage.history: Ancient pilgrimage sanctuary referenced in the Shiva Purana; destination of the world’s longest unassisted foot pilgrimage (Shravani Mela).
heritage.culture: Millions of Kanwariyas walk 105 km barefoot carrying holy Ganga water from Sultanganj to offer to the lingam in the holy month of Shravana.
heritage.best_time: October to March (Shravani Mela in July/August)

heritage.title: Basilica of Bom Jesus (Old Goa)
heritage.summary: UNESCO World Heritage 16th-century Jesuit Baroque basilica enshrining the mortal remains of Saint Francis Xavier in a silver casket.
heritage.history: Consecrated in May 1605, marking the onset of the Baroque style in India; holds the triennial or decennial Exposition of sacred relics.
heritage.culture: Constructed of red laterite stone with a gilded altar rising 54 feet, embellished with Italian marble flooring inlaid with precious stones.
heritage.best_time: October to April (Feast of St. Francis Xavier on 3 December)

heritage.title: Fort Aguada & 17th-Century Lighthouse
heritage.summary: Well-preserved 17th-century Portuguese fortress standing proudly on the headland overlooking the confluence of the Mandovi River and the Arabian Sea.
heritage.history: Erected in 1612 to protect against Dutch fleets and Maratha raids; named "Aguada" (Watering Place) after its freshwater spring that replenished passing merchant vessels.
heritage.culture: Features a massive subterranean cistern capable of holding 2.3 million gallons of fresh water, and one of Asia’s oldest four-storey rotary lighthouses.

heritage.title: Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial
heritage.summary: Historic public garden and solemn national memorial preserving bullet marks, the Martyrs’ Well, and the eternal flame of the Indian freedom struggle.
heritage.history: Site of the fateful massacre on Baisakhi, 13 April 1919, when British troops under General Dyer opened fire on unarmed peaceful demonstrators.
heritage.culture: A sacred touchstone of India’s fight for independence that ignited Mahatma Gandhi’s Non-Cooperation Movement.
heritage.timings: 06:30 AM - 07:30 PM (Sound & Light show at 07:00 PM)

heritage.title: Martand Sun Temple Ruins
heritage.summary: Colossal 8th-century stone temple ruins blending classical Greco-Roman, Gandharan, and Gupta architectural traditions on a scenic plateau.
heritage.history: Constructed by Emperor Lalitaditya Muktapida of the Karkota dynasty, who ruled an empire stretching from Punjab to Bengal.
heritage.culture: Enclosed by a grand colonnaded courtyard of 84 fluted pillars and Greek-style trefoil arch entrances dedicated to the sun god Surya.

heritage.title: Shalimar Bagh Mughal Gardens
heritage.summary: The crowning jewel of Mughal garden architecture, built on the northeast shores of Dal Lake with 4 cascading terraced water channels.
heritage.history: Laid out in 1619 by Mughal Emperor Jahangir for his beloved empress Nur Jahan, praised as "Farah Baksh" (The Delightful).
heritage.culture: Features black polished marble pavilions (Diwan-i-Khas), 410 fountains fed by mountain spring water, and centuries-old Chinar trees.
heritage.best_time: April to October (Autumn Chinar foliage in October/November)

heritage.title: Leh Royal Palace (Lhachen Palkhar)
heritage.summary: Nine-storey medieval royal palace rising over the historic bazaar of Leh, offering panoramic vistas of the Stok Kangri mountain range.
heritage.history: Constructed in the 17th century by King Sengge Namgyal of the Namgyal dynasty to serve as the seat of Ladakhi kings.
heritage.culture: Built using traditional mud bricks, timber beams, and stone without mortar, housing royal ceremonial garments and 450-year-old thangkas.

heritage.title: Hemis Gompa & Museum
heritage.summary: The largest and wealthiest Buddhist monastery in Ladakh, home to the world-famous annual Hemis Festival Cham masked dances.
heritage.history: Re-established in 1672 by King Sengge Namgyal and dedicated to the Drukpa Kagyu lineage of Tibetan Buddhism.
heritage.culture: Houses a subterranean museum holding golden statues, jewelled prayer wheels, and a giant silk thangka unfurled once every 12 years.
heritage.best_time: June to September (Hemis Festival in June/July)

heritage.title: Thiksey Monastery (Mini Potala)
heritage.summary: Grand 12-storey whitewashed Tibetan Buddhist monastery perched on a hill in the Indus Valley, famed for its 49-foot statue of Maitreya Buddha.
heritage.history: Founded in 1430 AD by Changsem Sherab Zangpo, a disciple of Je Tsongkhapa, founder of the Gelugpa (Yellow Hat) order.
heritage.culture: Features 10 temples, monastic residences for 120 monks, ancient Buddhist stupas, and early morning butter lamp chanting ceremonies.

heritage.title: Hidimba Devi Temple (Dhungari Temple)
heritage.summary: Four-tiered wooden pagoda sanctuary built around an ancient cave where Hidimba Devi, consort of Bhima from the Mahabharata, meditated.
heritage.history: Erected in 1553 AD by Raja Bahadur Singh amidst towering deodar cedars at the foothills of the Himalayas.
heritage.culture: Showcases indigenous Kathkuni timber-and-stone architecture, intricately carved wooden doors depicting deities, and horn motifs.
heritage.best_time: March to June, September to December

heritage.title: Tabo Monastery (Ajanta of the Himalayas)
heritage.summary: Millennium-old Tibetan Buddhist mud-brick gompa perched at 10,000 feet in Spiti Valley, housing pristine 10th-century wall frescoes and stucco statues.
heritage.history: Founded in 996 AD by the Buddhist King and lotsawa Ringchen Zangpo in the Kingdom of Guge.
heritage.culture: Preserves priceless Buddhist thangkas, manuscripts, and nine historic temples adorned with Kashmiri-influenced Gandhara Buddhist art.
heritage.location_name: Spiti Valley, Lahaul & Spiti, Himachal Pradesh

heritage.title: Jageshwar Dham Temple Complex
heritage.summary: A sacred cluster of 124 stone temples nestled in dense Himalayan deodar forests, considered one of the earliest seats of Lakulisha Shaivism.
heritage.history: Constructed between the 7th and 14th centuries CE by the Katyuri and Chand kings of Kumaon.
heritage.culture: Exhibits Nagara temple architecture with Shikhara spires, stone relief sculptures, and the ancient Mrityunjaya and Dandeshwar shrines.
heritage.best_time: April to June, September to November

heritage.title: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT)
heritage.summary: An outstanding example of Victorian Italianate Gothic Revival architecture merged with traditional Indian palace craftsmanship.
heritage.history: Designed by British architect F. W. Stevens and opened in 1888 to celebrate Queen Victoria’s Golden Jubilee as Victoria Terminus.
heritage.culture: Features an ornate stone dome, gargoyles, stained glass windows, and peacock carvings sculpted by Indian craftsmen of Sir J.J. School of Art.

heritage.title: Kalka–Shimla Mountain Toy Train
heritage.summary: UNESCO World Heritage 96-km narrow-gauge mountain railway ascending through 102 tunnels, 864 bridges, and pine-clad Himalayan ridges.
heritage.history: Built under British engineers and opened in 1903 to connect summer capital Shimla with the plains of Punjab.
heritage.culture: Celebrated engineering marvel offering panoramic vistas of the Shivalik range and traditional wooden colonial railway stations.
heritage.best_time: Year-round (Snow in winter, lush green in monsoon)

heritage.title: Kaziranga National Park & Elephant Grasslands
heritage.summary: UNESCO World Heritage ecological sanctuary holding two-thirds of the planet’s great one-horned rhinoceros population in Brahmaputra floodplains.
heritage.history: Created in 1905 through the conservation efforts of Mary Curzon; designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985.
heritage.culture: A global benchmark for wildlife conservation, populated by wild water buffaloes, swamp deer, Bengal tigers, and tribal Mishing settlements.
heritage.timings: Morning & Afternoon Jeep and Elephant Safaris (Nov to April)

heritage.title: Kerala Kalamandalam Performing Arts Centre
heritage.summary: The world-famous academy of Indian classical performing arts on the banks of the Bharathapuzha River.
heritage.history: Founded in 1930 by legendary poet Vallathol Narayana Menon to revive Kathakali, Mohiniyattam, and Koodiyattam (UNESCO Intangible Heritage).
heritage.culture: Follows traditional Gurukula pedagogy where disciples master Natyashastra facial expressions (Navarasas), mudras, and intricate chutti face makeup.

heritage.title: Khajuraho Group of Monuments
heritage.summary: Celebrated UNESCO world heritage cluster of Nagara-style Hindu and Jain sandstone temples adorned with sublime celestial sculptures.
heritage.history: Erected between 950 and 1050 AD by rulers of the Chandela dynasty; of the original 85 temples, 25 survive in remarkable preservation.
heritage.culture: Celebrates human emotions, spiritual transcendence, and architectural symmetry, climaxing in the soaring Kandariya Mahadeva Temple.
heritage.best_time: October to March (Khajuraho Dance Festival in February)

heritage.title: Sé Cathedral of Santa Catarina
heritage.summary: One of the largest church buildings in Asia, built in Portuguese-Manueline style, famed for the "Golden Bell" heard throughout Old Goa.
heritage.history: Commissioned by Afonso de Albuquerque to commemorate the Portuguese victory over an invading Muslim army in 1510 on Saint Catherine’s Day.
heritage.culture: Houses eight chapel altars, an ornate carved reredos depicting Catherine of Alexandria, and the Miraculous Cross of Jesus.

heritage.title: Shaniwar Wada Palace
heritage.summary: The seven-story fortified seat of the Peshwa prime ministers of the Maratha Empire, famed for the Delhi Darwaza spiked gates.
heritage.history: Foundation laid by Peshwa Baji Rao I on Saturday (Shaniwar), 10 January 1730, and completed in 1732.
heritage.culture: Witnessed the zenith of Maratha diplomacy across the subcontinent. Preserves massive perimeter walls with teakwood spiked anti-elephant gates.
heritage.timings: 09:00 AM - 05:30 PM, Sound & Light Show: 07:00 PM

heritage.title: Raigad Fort (Capital of Swarajya)
heritage.summary: The impregnable hill fortress perched 2,700 feet up in the Sahyadri mountains, chosen by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj as the royal capital.
heritage.history: Shivaji Maharaj captured the hill in 1656 and commissioned master architect Hiroji Indulkar to construct the royal court, granaries, and market.
heritage.culture: Site of the historic Coronation of Shivaji Maharaj in 1674 CE. Features the majestic Raj Sabha, Mena Darwaza, and the steep Maha Darwaza cliffside.

heritage.title: Bhoramdeo Temple (Khajuraho of Chhattisgarh)
heritage.summary: Exquisite 11th-century Nagar-style stone temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, set against the backdrop of the Maikal mountain range.
heritage.history: Constructed by King Ramchandra of the Nagavanshi dynasty between the 7th and 11th centuries CE.
heritage.culture: Decorated with ornate stone friezes depicting musicians, dancers, celestial nymphs, and mythological beasts carved in black basalt.
heritage.best_time: October to March (Bhoramdeo Mahotsav in March)

heritage.title: Badami Cave Temples
heritage.summary: Four magnificent rock-cut cave shrines carved out of red sandstone cliffs overlooking the sacred Agastya Lake.
heritage.history: Carved between the 6th and 8th centuries CE by the Early Chalukyas of Vatapi, representing the transition to free-standing temple architecture.
heritage.culture: Cave 1 features the famous 18-armed dancing Nataraja executing 81 Bharatanatyam poses simultaneously in high relief.

heritage.title: Bangaram Coral Atoll & Marine Biosphere
heritage.hindi_title: बंगाराम कोरल एटोल एवं मरीन बायोस्फीयर
heritage.summary: A breathtaking teardrop-shaped uninhabited coral atoll enclosed by an immense shallow turquoise lagoon and glowing bioluminescent night plankton.
heritage.history: Ancient seafaring landmark mentioned in classical Periplus of the Erythraean Sea guiding Arab and Roman spice merchants across the Indian Ocean.
heritage.culture: Strictly conserved marine biosphere home to green sea turtles, stingrays, manta rays, and over 120 species of multicolored live coral reefs.
heritage.timings: Boat excursions from Agatti Island (Daylight hours)

heritage.title: Barabar Caves (India’s Oldest Rock-Cut Caves)
heritage.summary: The oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India, carved with mirror-like polished granite surfaces and acoustic resonance echo chambers.
heritage.history: Excavated during the reign of Mauryan Emperor Ashoka (273–232 BCE) for ascetics of the ancient Ajivika sect.
