heritage.culture: Features Lomas Rishi Cave with Chaitya archways imitating timber architecture, inspiring E.M. Forster’s Marabar Caves in "A Passage to India".

heritage.title: Borra Caves & Araku Tribal Valley
heritage.summary: Subterranean million-year-old limestone karstic caverns penetrating 260 feet into the Ananthagiri hills of the Eastern Ghats.
heritage.history: Discovered in 1807 by British geologist William King; inhabited in prehistoric times with stone tools dating to the Upper Paleolithic era.
heritage.culture: Illuminated with colorful LEDs revealing bizarre natural stalactite and stalagmite formations resembling Shiva-Parvati, sages, and temple domes.
heritage.location_name: Alluri Sitharama Raju District, Andhra Pradesh

heritage.title: Brahma Sarovar & Jyotisar
heritage.summary: One of Asia’s largest sacred man-made water basins and the sacred site of Jyotisar where Lord Krishna delivered the Bhagavad Gita.
heritage.history: Vedic land where the great epic Mahabharata war was fought, praised in texts from the Rigveda to Al-Biruni’s Kitab-ul-Hind.
heritage.culture: Center for Gita Jayanti celebrations with half a million pilgrims performing Deep Daan across 3,600-foot sandstone bathing ghats.
heritage.best_time: October to March (International Gita Mahotsav in Dec)

heritage.title: Cheena Vala (Chinese Fishing Nets)
heritage.summary: Cantilevered shore-operated fishing nets lining Fort Kochi harbor, a testament to early Sino-Indian trade routes.
heritage.history: Introduced by Chinese explorer Zheng He’s fleet in the 14th century during the reign of the Kochi Maharajas.
heritage.culture: Operated by a team of six fishermen using counterweight stones on teakwood beams, silhouetted against glowing Arabian Sea sunsets.

heritage.title: Chitrakote Falls (The Niagara of India)
heritage.summary: India’s widest natural waterfall, plunging 98 feet across a 985-foot horseshoe cliff over the Indravati River in the heart of Bastar.
heritage.history: A sacred land steeped in Dandakaranya epic folklore where Lord Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana spent years of their exile.
heritage.culture: Surrounded by indigenous Gond and Maria tribal settlements celebrated for Dokra bell-metal bell casting and Bastar wooden crafts.
heritage.best_time: July to October for colossal water volume; Nov to Feb for clear turquoise pools

heritage.title: Diu Sea Fortress & Naida Caves
heritage.hindi_title: दीव समुद्री किला एवं नायडा गुफाएं
heritage.summary: Imposing 1535 Portuguese coastal sea fort bordered by three sea moats, flanked by the mystical, light-dappled subterranean Naida Caves.
heritage.history: Built following an alliance between Bahadur Shah of Gujarat and the Portuguese against Mughal Emperor Humayun, defended with bronze cannons.
heritage.culture: Features stone battlements, a Venetian-style lighthouse, St. Thomas Church museum, and sunlit limestone caverns carved by Portuguese stonemasons.
heritage.location_name: Diu Island, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

heritage.title: Dudhni Lake & Warli Tribal Heritage
heritage.hindi_title: दुधनी झील एवं वारली जनजातीय धरोहर
heritage.summary: Serene lakeside tribal cultural hub nestled beside the Madhuban Dam reservoir, home to the ancient earth-and-rice Warli painting tradition.
heritage.history: Cradle of indigenous Kokna and Warli tribes who have inhabited the Western Ghats foothills for over a millennium.
heritage.culture: Features traditional mud-walled round huts (Tarpa dance courtyards) decorated with white rice-paste geometric frescoes honoring Mother Nature (Palghat).
heritage.best_time: October to March (Tarpa Festival in December)

heritage.title: INA War Memorial & Netaji Flagstaff
heritage.summary: The historic soil where Colonel Shaukat Ali of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose’s Indian National Army first unfurled the Tricolour on Indian soil on 14 April 1944.
heritage.history: Headquarters of the Indo-Japanese offensive during the Burma Campaign, holding Netaji’s personal artifacts and battle journals.
heritage.culture: Preserves the bronze statue of Netaji, a replica of the INA Singapore memorial, and exhibits celebrating the Azad Hind movement.

heritage.title: Ita Fort (Fort of Bricks)
heritage.summary: Historic 14th-century fortress constructed using 8 million hand-baked earthen bricks, which gave Arunachal Pradesh’s capital Itanagar its name.
heritage.history: Built by the kings of the medieval Chutiya dynasty as an eastern bastion commanding trade routes through the Dikrong River valley.
heritage.culture: Surrounded by lush orchids and steep natural ramparts, showcasing ancient engineering adapting to high-rainfall Sub-Himalayan jungles.

heritage.title: Kangla Fort (Ancient Citadel of Manipur)
heritage.summary: The revered ancient royal seat of Meitei monarchs on the banks of the Imphal River, dating back to 33 CE.
heritage.history: Religious and political nerve center of Manipur until its annexation by the British following the Anglo-Manipur War of 1891.
heritage.culture: Enshrines sacred Govindaji Temple, dragon-lion monoliths (Kangla Sha), and sacred ponds where coronation rituals took place.

heritage.title: Kedarnath Jyotirlinga Dham
heritage.summary: The highest of the 12 Jyotirlingas, nestled at 3,583 metres in the Garhwal Himalayas near the Mandakini River glacier.
heritage.history: Believed to have been originally built by the Pandavas and rejuvenated by Adi Shankaracharya in the 8th century CE.
heritage.culture: Constructed of massive interlocking grey stone slabs that miraculously withstood the catastrophic 2013 Himalayan deluge.
heritage.timings: 04:00 AM - 09:00 PM (Akshaya Tritiya to Kartik Purnima)
heritage.best_time: May to June, September to October

heritage.title: Khonoma Green & Angami Warrior Village
heritage.summary: Asia’s first community-declared Green Village, famed for its terraced rice paddies, traditional stone forts, and Angami tribal craftsmanship.
heritage.history: Renowned for fiercely resisting British colonial forces in three major military battles between 1850 and 1879.
heritage.culture: A global model of community-led conservation where villagers banned hunting and timber felling to save the endangered Blyth’s tragopan pheasant.

heritage.title: Kohima War Cemetery & Battle Ridge
heritage.summary: Solemn World War II memorial dedicated to soldiers who halted the Japanese invasion of India in 1944 on the Deputy Commissioner’s tennis court.
heritage.history: The Battle of Kohima was voted by Britain’s National Army Museum as "Britain’s Greatest Battle", turning the tide of the Burma Campaign.
heritage.culture: Famous for the Kohima Epitaph: "When you go home, tell them of us and say, For your tomorrow, we gave our today."

heritage.title: Malinithan Archaeological Granite Temple
heritage.summary: A 14th-century archaeological temple mound built of carved granite stone blocks depicting celestial dancers and erotic figures.
heritage.history: Associated with the legend of Lord Krishna and Rukmini visiting the hermit sage Parashurama and Goddess Malini (Parvati).
heritage.culture: Demonstrates early trans-Himalayan trade routes and cultural synthesis between the Brahmaputra plains and Arunachal tribes.

heritage.title: Maluti Terracotta Temple Village
heritage.summary: A fairytale heritage village holding 72 surviving 17th-century terracotta temples depicting scenes from Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Chandi Mahatmya.
heritage.history: Built by the Nankar royal dynasty of King Basanta Roy, who endowed artisans to carve temples instead of constructing royal palaces.
heritage.culture: Showcases traditional Char-Chala architecture with intricate burnt clay plaques depicting Goddess Durga combating Mahishasura.
heritage.best_time: October to March (Kali Puja in October)

heritage.title: Matrimandir (Soul of Auroville)
heritage.summary: A futuristic golden geodesic sphere dedicated to universal human unity, surrounded by 12 tranquil lotus petal gardens and peaceful meditation spaces.
heritage.history: Inaugurated in 1968 by Mirra Alfassa (The Mother), spiritual collaborator of Sri Aurobindo, with youth from 124 nations depositing soil from their homelands.
heritage.culture: Inside the inner white marble chamber, a single ray of sunlight is directed by a heliostat mirror through a 70-cm optically perfect crystal globe.
heritage.timings: 09:00 AM - 04:30 PM (Prior booking required for inner chamber)

heritage.title: Mawlynnong Village & Sky Walk
heritage.summary: Celebrated across the world as "God’s Own Garden" and Asia’s cleanest village, guided by 100% Khasi community eco-cleanliness traditions.
heritage.history: Maintained for over a century with bamboo dustbins at every lane, community composting, and matrilineal village council stewardship.
heritage.culture: Offers the 85-foot bamboo Sky Walk viewing platform extending over the lush canopies of Bangladesh plains.

heritage.title: Meenakshi Amman Temple
heritage.summary: Spiritual epicentre of 2,500-year-old Madurai, celebrated for its 14 towering polychrome gopurams and Hall of a Thousand Pillars.
heritage.history: Ancient roots dating to Sangam times; reconstructed and expanded during the 16th and 17th centuries under King Tirumala Nayaka.
heritage.culture: Dedicated to Goddess Meenakshi (a manifestation of Parvati) and Sundareswarar. The Hall of 1000 Pillars features musical pillars that emit distinct notes when struck.

heritage.title: Minicoy Historic 1885 Lighthouse
heritage.summary: A soaring 162-foot white masonry brick lighthouse built by the British to guide international merchant spice ships navigating the Eight Degree Channel.
heritage.history: Inaugurated on 2 February 1885 by the London Trinity House; offers breathtaking 360-degree views of coral reefs and turquoise atolls.
heritage.culture: Minicoy possesses a unique Mahl culture with traditional seamanship, multi-tiered tribal villages (Athiris), and ancient Jahadhoni longboats.

heritage.title: Moti Daman Fort & St. Jerome Bastion
heritage.summary: Massive polygonal polygon fortress spanning 30,000 sq metres with 10 bastions on the southern bank of the Daman Ganga River.
heritage.history: Constructed by the Portuguese in 1559 following the seizure of Daman from the Sultan of Gujarat, guarded by a deep sea moat.
heritage.culture: Encloses the 17th-century Cathedral of Bom Jesus, the Convent of the Dominican Order, and ancient Portuguese cobblestone alleys.

heritage.title: Neermahal (Twijilikma Water Palace)
heritage.summary: The only lake palace in Eastern and Northeastern India, built in the middle of Rudrasagar Lake blending Hindu and Islamic architectural motifs.
heritage.history: Constructed between 1930 and 1938 by Maharaja Bir Bikram Kishore Manikya as his summer residence.
heritage.culture: Accessible by boat; illuminated like a fairytale castle during evening light shows, with red-and-white domes reflecting on the waters.
heritage.best_time: October to March (Neermahal Water Festival in September)

heritage.title: Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose (Ross) Island
heritage.summary: An evocative ghost island where Victorian colonial ballrooms, printing presses, and church ruins are being reclaimed by strangler fig tree roots.
heritage.history: Former administrative headquarters of the Andaman penal settlement; liberated by the Japanese in 1943 where Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose hoisted the Tricolour.
heritage.culture: Spotted deer and peacocks roam freely through century-old mossy stone arches overlooking the turquoise waters of the Bay of Bengal.
heritage.location_name: South Andaman, Andaman and Nicobar Islands

heritage.title: Nohkalikai Falls & Cherrapunji Gorges
heritage.summary: The tallest plunge waterfall in India (1,115 feet), cascading into a deep emerald plunge pool surrounded by misty Meghalayan rainforests.
heritage.history: Immortalized in Khasi oral mythology about Likai, a grief-stricken mother who leapt from the plateau rim above the gorge.
heritage.culture: Located in Sohra (Cherrapunji), one of the wettest places on Earth, flanked by natural limestone caves and sacred tribal groves.
heritage.best_time: September to December (clear views), June to August (heavy monsoon rush)

heritage.title: Pemayangtse Monastery (Perfect Sublime Lotus)
heritage.summary: One of Sikkim’s premier Nyingma monasteries, commanding majestic vistas of sacred Mount Kangchenjunga.
heritage.history: Founded in 1705 by Lama Lhatsun Chempo, designed exclusively for monks belonging to the Bhutia community.
heritage.culture: Famed for "Sangtok Palri", a 7-tiered wooden celestial palace carved over 5 years by Dungzin Rinpoche depicting Guru Padmasambhava’s paradise.
heritage.best_time: October to May (Cham Masked Dance in February)

heritage.title: Rabdentse Palace & Royal Stupa Ruins
heritage.summary: The historic second capital of the Kingdom of Sikkim from 1670 to 1814, framed by sacred deodar trees and snow peaks of Kangchenjunga.
heritage.history: Established by Chogyal Tensung Namgyal after Yuksom; destroyed during the Nepalese Gorkha invasions in 1814.
heritage.culture: Preserves the royal stone throne, the King’s palace foundations, and the Namphogang stone stupas overlooking deep valleys.

heritage.title: Radhanagar Beach & Coral Reefs (Havelock)
heritage.summary: Crowned as the best beach in Asia by Time Magazine, famed for powder-white sands, gentle azure surf, and magnificent tropical sunset views.
heritage.history: Part of Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island) named in honour of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose who declared Andaman liberated in 1943.
heritage.culture: Blue Flag certified eco-beach backed by lush mahua rainforest canopies, preserving pristine turtle nesting grounds and vibrant coral beds.
heritage.location_name: Swaraj Dweep (Havelock), Andaman and Nicobar Islands

heritage.title: Rang Ghar (Ahom Royal Amphitheatre)
heritage.summary: Two-storey royal sports pavilion shaped like an inverted Ahom royal longboat, considered one of Asia’s earliest sporting amphitheatres.
heritage.history: Commissioned in 1744–1751 AD by Ahom King Swargadeo Pramatta Singha to witness buffalo fights and traditional Rongali Bihu performances.
heritage.culture: Built with thin burnt indigenous bricks cemented using a traditional mortar of sticky rice (Bora Saul) and duck eggs.
heritage.best_time: October to April (Rongali Bihu in April)

heritage.title: Shankaracharya Temple (Gopadari Hill)
heritage.summary: Historic stone temple dedicated to Lord Shiva resting atop Gopadari Hill at 1,000 feet above Srinagar, offering bird’s-eye views of Dal Lake.
heritage.history: Dates back to 200 BCE, visited and sanctified by philosopher Adi Shankaracharya during his tour of Kashmir in the 8th century.
heritage.culture: Built on a high octagonal plinth with horseshoe arch vaults and ancient Persian and Sanskrit inscriptions.

heritage.title: Sirpur Archaeological Heritage Site
heritage.summary: Ancient riverbank capital of the Sarabhapuriya and Somavamsi dynasties, featuring the 7th-century red-brick Laxman Temple.
heritage.history: Visited in 639 CE by Chinese scholar Xuanzang who recorded over 100 Buddhist monasteries housing 10,000 monks living in harmony with Vedic scholars.
heritage.culture: Famous for carved brick mouldings depicting Vishnu’s incarnations, Krishna Lila reliefs, and underground Buddhist viharas.
heritage.best_time: October to March (Sirpur National Dance Festival in January)

heritage.title: Solomon’s Temple of Aizawl
heritage.summary: Monumental white marble cathedral constructed over two decades, accommodating 10,000 worshipers within pristine landscaped gardens.
heritage.history: Conceived in 1984 by Kohhran Thianghlim (The Holy Church) and built using white marble imported from Makrana, Rajasthan.
heritage.culture: Features four soaring towers symbolizing the four pillars of faith, flanked by poly-carbonate sky vaults and cedar wood carvings.

heritage.title: Sri Aurobindo Ashram & Manakula Vinayagar
heritage.hindi_title: श्री अरबिंदो आश्रम एवं मनाकुला विनायक
heritage.summary: A world-famous spiritual sanctuary founded in 1926 by Sri Aurobindo and Mirra Alfassa, adjoining the ancient 500-year-old golden shrine of Lord Ganesha.
heritage.history: Served as the epicenter of Integral Yoga (Purna Yoga); the Samadhi marble tomb rests in a central courtyard shaded by the Service Tree.
heritage.culture: Preserves silence, meditation halls, international spiritual publishing presses, and hand-made paper and agarbatti artisan studios.
heritage.best_time: October to March (Darshan days in February, April, August, November)

heritage.title: Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple (Tirupati)
heritage.summary: The richest and most visited Hindu temple in the world, dedicated to Lord Vishnu as Venkateswara on the sacred Venkatadri hill of the Seshachalam range.
heritage.history: Patronized by Pallavas, Cholas, Pandyas, and most lavishly by Vijayanagara Emperor Krishnadevaraya who coated the Ananda Nilayam tower in gold.
heritage.culture: Celebrated for the sacred Tirupati Laddu (awarded a Geographical Indication tag) and daily head-tonsuring offerings representing detachment.

heritage.title: Ujjayanta Palace (Tripura State Museum)
heritage.summary: Splendid Neoclassical white royal palace surrounded by Mughal gardens and two reflecting lakes, named by Nobel Laureate Rabindranath Tagore.
heritage.history: Built in 1899–1901 by Maharaja Radha Kishore Manikya of the Manikya dynasty, which ruled Tripura continuously for over 500 years.
heritage.culture: Houses 22 galleries displaying rare archaeological sculptures, royal thrones, coins of the Manikya kings, and tribal Northeast artifacts.

heritage.title: Ujra Mosque & Intricate Floral Woodcarvings
heritage.summary: Exquisite 17th-century coral-stone mosque famous for its ceiling intricately carved from single pieces of indigenous timber with no nails.
heritage.history: Constructed by Sheikh Mohammad Kasim in the 17th century; water from the adjoining well is revered by islanders for its medicinal purity.
heritage.culture: Showcases traditional Lakshadweep maritime architecture where island master carpenters combined Arabic motifs with local coconut timber craft.

heritage.title: Unakoti Heritage Bas-Reliefs
heritage.summary: Colossal 7th-9th century Shaivite rock carvings sculpted across a steep forested ravine, known as the "Angkor Wat of the Northeast".
heritage.history: Legend holds there are "Unakoti" (one less than a crore / 99,99,999) rock-carved statues created when Lord Shiva spent the night on his journey to Kashi.
heritage.culture: Features the colossal 30-foot head of Unakotiswara Kal Bhairava with a 10-foot headdress flanked by Goddess Ganga riding a Capricorn.
heritage.best_time: October to April (Ashokastami Mela in April)

heritage.title: Vantawng Khawhthla Waterfalls
heritage.summary: The highest two-tiered waterfall in Mizoram (750 feet), rushing down thick bamboo hills on the Vanva River near Thenzawl handloom town.
heritage.history: Named after Vantawnga, a legendary Mizo swimmer praised in oral folklore for his miraculous aquatic prowess at the base of the cascade.
heritage.culture: Surrounded by protected virgin forests and traditional Mizo weavers who produce exquisite hand-spun "Puan" tribal wraps.

heritage.title: Vembanad Backwaters & Kettuvallam Heritage
heritage.summary: A labyrinthine network of tranquil lagoons, canals, and traditional wooden houseboats stitched together with coir ropes without nails.
heritage.history: Kettuvallams were historically rice barges transporting harvest from Kuttanad to ports, now adapted into sustainable cultural heritage cruisers.
heritage.culture: Demonstrates ancient boat-building mastery using Anjili wood, coir fiber, and fish oil coatings. Hub of the world-famous Nehru Trophy Boat Race.

heritage.title: Virasat-e-Khalsa
heritage.summary: Architectural wonder designed by Moshe Safdie, celebrating 500 years of Sikh history and the 300th anniversary of the Khalsa Panth.
heritage.history: Inaugurated in November 2011 at holy Anandpur Sahib, recognized as one of the most visited single-day museums in the Indian subcontinent.
heritage.culture: Features hand-crafted exhibits, glowing tapestry vaults, interactive audio guides, and soaring sandstone petals echoing the surrounding cliffs.
heritage.best_time: October to March (Hola Mohalla in March)

heritage.title: White Town / French Quarter Promenade
heritage.summary: Colonial Franco-Tamil heritage precinct with mustard-yellow villas, archways, bougainvillea balconies, and the 1.5-km seaside Goubert Promenade.
heritage.history: Laid out in an orderly grid plan by French Governor François Dupleix in the 18th century as the commercial headquarters of the French East India Company.
heritage.culture: Features the French War Memorial, statue of Joan of Arc, the Sri Aurobindo Ashram, and sea-facing colonial cafes serving baguettes and filter coffee.
heritage.timings: Open 24 hours (Vehicle-free seaside promenade after 05:00 PM)

heritage.title: Yadavindra Gardens (Pinjore)
heritage.summary: Historic 17th-century terraced Mughal garden complex featuring symmetrical water canals, splashing fountains, and royal pleasure palaces.
heritage.history: Designed by Nawab Fidai Khan, architect to Emperor Aurangzeb, and later refurbished by the Maharaja of Patiala.
heritage.culture: Laid out over 7 descending stepped terraces with the Sheesh Mahal, Rang Mahal, and Jal Mahal illuminated during summer Mango Festivals.

foods.name: Dal Baati Churma
foods.description: Crispy hard-baked wheat flour balls dipped generously in desi ghee, served with spicy mixed Panchmel dal and sweet powdered jaggery-wheat churma.

foods.name: Gatte ki Sabzi
foods.description: Spiced gram flour (besan) dumplings poached and simmered in a luscious curd and coriander gravy, native to Marwari desert kitchens.

foods.name: Jaipuri Malai Ghevar
foods.description: Disc-shaped honeycomb sweet pastry soaked in cardamom sugar syrup, topped with rich rabdi, saffron strands, and silver vark.

foods.name: Traditional Kerala Sadya
foods.description: Grand vegetarian banquet of 24–28 dishes served on plantain leaves, featuring Avial, Thoran, Olan, Sambar, Rasam, and creamy Parippu Payasam.

foods.name: Appam with Coconut Vegetable Stew
foods.description: Fermented rice and coconut milk pancakes with soft spongy centers and crispy lace borders, paired with aromatic coconut milk vegetable stew.

foods.name: Kanchipuram Kovil Idli
foods.description: Ancient temple offering steamed in Mandharai leaves with ginger, cumin, pepper, and pure cow ghee, celebrated in Sangam verses.

foods.name: Chettinad Seeraga Samba Biryani
foods.description: Fragrant short-grain seeraga samba rice cooked with stone-ground roasted spices, star anise, and fresh mint leaves.

foods.name: Awadhi Dum Pukht Biryani
foods.description: Aromatic basmati rice and tender morsels cooked in sealed handis over gentle charcoal embers with saffron, kewra, and green cardamom.

foods.name: Kolhapuri Misal Pav
foods.description: Fiery sprouted moth bean curry garnished with farsan, diced onions, and lime, accompanied by warm butter-toasted pav.

foods.name: Bengali Macher Jhol
foods.description: Comforting, fragrant freshwater carp or Rohu curry with tender potato wedges, flavored with Panch Phoron five-spice and turmeric.

foods.name: Banglar Rosogolla
foods.description: Spongy snow-white cottage cheese (Chhena) dumplings simmered in clarified light sugar syrup, carrying a GI tag for Bengal.

foods.name: Dhuska with Black Chickpea Ghugni
foods.description: Crispy deep-fried savory bread prepared from stone-ground fermented rice and chana dal batter, tempered with cumin and paired with spicy black chickpea curry (Ghugni).

foods.name: Wild Rugda / Phutka Forest Mushroom Curry
foods.description: Rare indigenous wild puffball mushrooms harvested only during monsoon beneath Sal tree roots, slow-cooked in cold-pressed mustard oil with garlic and whole rustic spices.

foods.name: Chilka Roti with Tomato Chutney
foods.description: Delicate traditional crepe prepared from soaked rice and chana dal batter, roasted on earthen tawas with minimal oil, served during tribal harvest festivals.

foods.name: Bihari Litti Chokha with Desi Ghee
foods.description: Whole wheat dough balls stuffed with spiced roasted gram flour (Sattu), baked over cow-dung embers, dipped in pure desi ghee, served with roasted eggplant-tomato-potato mash (Chokha).

foods.name: GI-Tagged Silao Khaja
foods.description: GI-tagged 52-layered crispy golden sweet made from wheat flour and sugar syrup, famously consumed in ancient Nalanda and Rajgir since the Mauryan era.

foods.name: Hyderabadi Dum Biryani
foods.description: World-renowned royal creation combining fragrant aged Basmati rice, marinated tender meat, saffron, fried onions (Birista), and mint, slow-cooked under dough seal (Dum).

foods.name: GI-Tagged Hyderabadi Royal Haleem
foods.description: Nutritious Ramzan delicacy slow-cooked for 12 hours in large copper cauldrons (Bhattis) blending pounded wheat, lentils, mutton, pure ghee, and 24 secret spices into a rich porridge.

foods.name: Atreyapuram Pootharekulu (Paper Sweet)
foods.description: GI-tagged paper-thin edible rice starch wrappers folded with pure ghee, powdered jaggery, cardamom, and chopped dry fruits.

foods.name: Andhra Gongura Mutton & Pachadi
foods.description: Iconic tangy and spicy preparation made from sorrel leaves (Gongura) stone-pounded with red chillies, garlic, and mustard seeds.

foods.name: Assamese Masor Tenga
foods.description: Light and refreshing tangy freshwater river fish curry cooked with tomatoes, Ou Tenga (elephant apple) or dried lemon, tempered with fenugreek.

foods.name: Koldil Paro (Banana Flower with Pigeon Meat)
foods.description: Ancient Ahom royal delicacy combining finely shredded banana blossom with spiced meat and whole black peppercorns.

foods.name: Chhena Poda (Roasted Cottage Cheese Cake)
foods.description: Traditional baked dessert of Odisha made by kneading fresh cottage cheese, semolina, cardamom, and caramelized sugar, wrapped in Sal leaves and baked in clay kilns.

foods.name: Puri Temple Dalma
foods.description: Sacred nutritious dish offered in Puri Jagannath Mahaprasad, prepared with toor dal, raw banana, pumpkin, papaya, tempered with Pancha Phutana and roasted cumin-chilli powder.

foods.name: Bengali Shorshe Ilish (Hilsa in Mustard Gravy)
foods.description: Pride of Bengali cuisine: fresh silver Hilsa fish steamed in stone-ground yellow and black mustard paste, green chillies, and pungent pure mustard oil.

foods.name: Bengali Mishti Doi in Earthen Pots
foods.description: Fermented caramelized sweet curd prepared by slow-reducing cow milk with palm jaggery (Nolen Gur) and setting it in porous terracotta pots for natural earthen flavor.

foods.name: Dal Baati Churma Platter
foods.description: Hard whole wheat balls baked over cow-dung cake embers and drowned in pure ghee, served with five-lentil panchmel dal and sweet cardamom churma.

foods.name: Pachkoota / Ker Sangri
foods.description: Authentic desert delicacy made with dried wild caper berries (Ker) and desert bean pods (Sangri) sauteed in mustard oil, red chillies, and amchur.

foods.name: Kerala Appam with Coconut Milk Vegetable Stew
foods.description: Fermented rice and coconut hoppers with crispy lace edges and soft pillowy centers, paired with a mild, aromatic coconut milk stew.

foods.name: Royal Mysore Pak
foods.description: Melt-in-mouth royal sweet created in the kitchens of Mysore Palace in 1935, made with roasted besan, copious pure desi ghee, and cardamom sugar syrup.

foods.name: Bisi Bele Bath
foods.description: Traditional Mysore dish meaning "hot lentil rice", prepared with aromatic spices, tamarind, toasted coconut, roasted cashews, and seasonal vegetables.

foods.name: Makki Di Roti & Sarson Ka Saag
foods.hindi_name: मक्के की रोटी एवं सरसों का साग
foods.description: Iconic Punjabi winter feast consisting of stone-ground cornmeal flatbreads served with slow-cooked mustard and bathua greens, topped with freshly churned white butter and jaggery.

foods.name: Surti Undhiyu with Puri
foods.description: Winter mixed vegetable potpourri of Surti papdi beans, baby eggplants, purple yam, and fenugreek muthias slow-cooked upside down in earthen pots.

foods.name: Maharashtrian Puran Poli with Katachi Amti
foods.description: Festive sweet flatbread stuffed with soft mashed chana dal and organic jaggery infused with nutmeg and cardamom, roasted in desi ghee.

foods.name: Indori Poha with Crispy Jalebi & Sev
foods.description: Steamed flattened rice spiced with fennel seeds and special Jeeravan masala, garnished with Ratlami Sev, pomegranate pearls, and paired with hot saffron jalebis.

foods.name: Authentic Kashmiri Rogan Josh
foods.description: Flagship jewel of the Kashmiri Wazwan, stewed with Kashmiri deggi mirch, fennel powder, ginger, and wild cockscomb flower extract (Ratan Jot) for crimson glow.

foods.name: Kashmiri Saffron Kahwa Tea
foods.description: Aromatic green tea brewed in brass Samovars with whole green cardamom, cinnamon quills, crushed almonds, and pure Pampore saffron strands.

foods.name: Goan Fish Curry with Coconut & Kokum
foods.description: Staple coastal curry cooked with freshly grated coconut, Kashmiri red chillies, coriander seeds, and tart dried kokum rind.

foods.name: Traditional Goan Bebinca
foods.description: Regal Indo-Portuguese pudding consisting of 7 to 16 caramelized layers baked with coconut milk, egg yolks, flour, sugar, and nutmeg.

foods.name: Pahari Kafuli (Spinach & Fenugreek Stew)
foods.description: Rich iron-loaded Himalayan delicacy made by slow-cooking wild mountain spinach and fenugreek leaves, thickened with rice paste in iron kadhais.

foods.name: Haryanvi Bajra Khichdi with Homemade White Butter
foods.description: Hearty winter porridge made from coarsely pounded pearl millet and yellow moong dal, served with generous dollops of fresh tindi ghee or butter and jaggery.

foods.name: Old Delhi Parathe Wali Gali Platter
foods.description: Deep-fried golden flatbreads stuffed with spiced cottage cheese, rabdi, bitter gourd, or potatoes, served with pumpkin sabzi, mint chutney, and tamarind saunth.

festivals.name: Pushkar Camel Fair
festivals.significance: One of the world’s largest camel and livestock fairs combined with holy pilgrimage baths in sacred Pushkar Lake.
festivals.celebration_style: Decorated camel beauty contests, Rajasthani folk dances, hot-air ballooning, and sacred evening Maha Aarti.

festivals.name: Onam Harvest & Homecoming
festivals.significance: Welcoming the mythical benevolent King Mahabali back to Kerala; marks prosperity and egalitarian harmony.
festivals.celebration_style: Floral carpet designs (Pookkalam), Pulikkali tiger dance, Onasadya grand banquet, and Vallamkali boat races.

festivals.name: Pongal Thanksgiving Harvest Festival
festivals.significance: Four-day thanksgiving festival dedicating harvests to Surya (Sun God), cattle (Mattu Pongal), and Mother Nature.
festivals.celebration_style: Boiling freshly harvested rice and milk in clay pots until it overflows shouting "Pongalo Pongal", Kolam chalk art, and Jallikattu.

festivals.name: Kumbh Mela Prayagraj
festivals.significance: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage; the largest congregation of humanity bathing at the holy Triveni Sangam.
festivals.celebration_style: Royal bathing processions (Shahi Snan) of Akharas, holy discourses, Vedic chanting, and sea of illuminated pilgrim tents.

festivals.name: Ganeshotsav
festivals.significance: Re-popularized by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak in 1893 to unite citizens against colonial rule through community spirit.
festivals.celebration_style: Grand community pandals (Lalbaugcha Raja), rhythmic Dhol-Tasha troop beats, and ocean immersion (Visarjan) processions.

festivals.name: Kolkata Durga Puja
festivals.significance: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, celebrating the victory of Goddess Durga over evil Mahishasura.
festivals.celebration_style: Vast open-air artistic theme pandals transforming the city into a global art gallery, Dhunuchi dance, and Sindoor Khela.

festivals.name: Sarhul Nature & Sal Blossom Festival
festivals.significance: Most sacred indigenous tribal festival of Oraon, Munda, Ho, and Santhal communities worshipping Mother Earth (Dharti Maa) and the blooming Sal tree in sacred Sarna groves.
festivals.celebration_style: Pahan village priests offer three roosters and water pitchers to predict monsoon rainfall, while men and women dance in circles to the rhythmic beats of Mandar, Dhol, and Nagada.

festivals.name: Karam / Karma Tribal Festival
festivals.significance: Celebrates youth, agricultural fertility, and brotherhood through the ritual worship of the sacred Karam tree branch planted in the Akhra dancing ground.
festivals.celebration_style: Young unmarried women observe strict day-long fasts, germinating Java barley shoots in bamboo baskets, followed by all-night Jhumair singing and dancing.

festivals.name: Mahaparva Chhath Puja
festivals.significance: Rigorous 4-day solar and cosmic nature veneration dedicated to Lord Surya and Chhathi Maiya for longevity, prosperity, family well-being, and purity of soul.
festivals.celebration_style: Vratis stand waist-deep in holy rivers to offer Arghya (oblations) to the setting and rising sun with bamboo soop filled with Thekua, sugarcane, and seasonal fruits.

festivals.name: Rongali / Bohag Bihu
festivals.significance: Assamese festival of joy, fertility, and agricultural sowing marking the onset of spring and the seeding of paddy fields.
festivals.celebration_style: Youth gather outdoors to dance in circles to the rhythmic beats of the Dhol, Pepa (buffalo horn flute), and Gogona (bamboo jaw harp).

festivals.name: Kamakhya Ambubachi Mela
festivals.significance: Annual tantric congregation celebrating the yearly menstrual cycle of Mother Earth at the sanctum of Goddess Kamakhya on Nilachal Hill.
festivals.celebration_style: Temple doors remain closed for 3 days while thousands of Sadhus and devotees chant hymns, concluding with the distribution of sacred Raktovastra red cloth.

festivals.name: Bathukamma Floral Festival
festivals.significance: Celebrates womanhood, nature, and Mother Gauri through elaborate seasonal flower arrangements shaped as temple towers.
festivals.celebration_style: Women dressed in traditional Langa Voni sing ancient folk songs in circles around floral towers before immersing them in local lakes.

festivals.name: Sammakka Sarakka Medaram Jathara
festivals.significance: Asia’s largest tribal congregation commemorating the historic battle of mother-daughter warriors Sammakka and Sarakka against Kakatiya oppression.
festivals.celebration_style: Over 10 million pilgrims offer their body-weight in jaggery (called Bangaram / Gold) to tree sanctums in the dense Eturnagaram forest.

festivals.name: Ugadi (Telugu New Year)
festivals.significance: Astronomical beginning of the Telugu lunar new year, marked by the ceremonial reading of the Panchanga predictions.
festivals.celebration_style: Families prepare Ugadi Pachadi, a unique preparation combining sweet, sour, salty, bitter, tangy, and spicy tastes reflecting life’s diverse experiences.

festivals.name: Puri Jagannath Ratha Yatra
festivals.significance: The world’s oldest and largest annual chariot procession, where Lord Jagannath, Balabhadra, and Subhadra journey to Gundicha Temple.
festivals.celebration_style: Millions of devotees pull massive 45-foot hand-carved wooden chariots through the Grand Bada Danda road with cymbals and conches.

festivals.name: Onam & Vallam Kali (Boat Race)
festivals.significance: Celebrates the mythical homecoming of the benevolent Daitya King Mahabali and the bountiful state harvest.
festivals.celebration_style: Elaborate Pookkalam floral carpets at doorways, 26-dish Onasadya banquets on plantain leaves, and high-speed Snake Boat Races (Chundan Vallam).

festivals.name: Thrissur Pooram (Mother of all Poorams)
festivals.significance: Grand 200-year-old temple pageant instituted by Sakthan Thampuran featuring competitive display of caparisoned elephants and umbrellas.
festivals.celebration_style: Ilanjithara Melam percussion symphony with over 250 chenda drummers and breathtaking Kudamattam umbrella shifting.

festivals.name: Thai Pongal & Jallikattu
festivals.significance: Four-day Tamil harvest thanksgiving honoring the Sun God Surya, rain gods, and agricultural cattle.
festivals.celebration_style: Boiling newly harvested rice and milk in earthen pots until it overflows shouting "Pongalo Pongal", Kolam designs, and bull-embracing Jallikattu.

festivals.name: Baisakhi Harvest Festival
festivals.significance: Marks the golden wheat harvest and commemorates the founding of the Khalsa Panth by Guru Gobind Singh Ji in 1699.
festivals.celebration_style: Nagar Kirtan religious processions, visits to Gurdwaras for Karah Parshad, and vigorous energetic Bhangra performances.

festivals.name: Navratri Mahotsav & Rann Utsav
festivals.significance: The world’s longest dance festival honoring Goddess Durga across nine nights of devotional joy and Shakti worship.
festivals.celebration_style: Hundreds of thousands dressed in mirror-work Chaniya Cholis perform synchronized Garba clapping around illuminated sanctums till dawn.

festivals.name: Pushkar International Camel & Cultural Fair
festivals.significance: Ancient religious pilgrimage where devotees take holy dips in sacred Pushkar Lake and trade embellished livestock.
festivals.celebration_style: Mustache competitions, bridal dress contests, desert camel races, and thousands of oil lamps floating on the lake under the full moon.

festivals.name: Hornbill Festival (Festival of Festivals)
festivals.significance: A majestic grand gathering uniting all 17 recognized indigenous Naga tribes to preserve and celebrate their ancestral warrior heritage.
festivals.celebration_style: Traditional Morung dormitory village showcases, ancient war chants, log-drum beating, indigenous games, and tribal feasts at Kisama.

festivals.name: Angami Sekrenyi Purification Festival
festivals.significance: 10-day ritual purification festival of the Angami Nagas to cleanse past sins and renew body and soul for the upcoming year.
festivals.celebration_style: Men cleanse themselves at village wells before dawn, wear ceremonial warrior kilts with hornbill feathers, and feast on traditional brew.

festivals.name: Hemis Gompa Monastery Festival
festivals.significance: Celebrates the birth anniversary of Guru Padmasambhava (Guru Rinpoche), who brought Vajrayana Buddhism to the trans-Himalayas.
festivals.celebration_style: Monks perform mystical sacred Cham mask dances wearing brocade robes and silk scarves to the clash of long horns and cymbals.

festivals.name: International Kullu Dussehra
festivals.significance: Unique 7-day celestial congregation dating back to the 17th century when King Jagat Singh consecrated Lord Raghunath.
festivals.celebration_style: Over 200 village deities (Devtas) arrive from surrounding valleys in ornate wooden palanquins to camp at Dhalpur Maidan.

festivals.name: Kolkata Durga Puja Festival
festivals.month_or_season: September - October (Ashwin Shukla Shashthi to Dashami)
festivals.significance: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity celebrating the triumph of Mother Durga over tyranny.
festivals.celebration_style: Thousands of artistically sculpted theme pandals across the city, synchronized Dhunuchi smoke dance, and joyous Sindoor Khela.

festivals.name: Maharashtra Ganeshotsav
festivals.significance: Mass community celebration revived by Lokmanya Tilak in 1893 to unite citizens through cultural unity and spiritual devotion.
festivals.celebration_style: Massive clay murtis consecrated in Sarvajanik pandals, intense Dhol-Tasha troop performances, and Visarjan processions chanting "Ganpati Bappa Morya".

languages.name: Gujarati (ગુજરાતી)
languages.greeting: Kem Chho / Jai Shri Krishna (જય શ્રી કૃષ્ણ)
